author: Potuz
subject: Bound data-column availability wait during batch sync (#16978)
body:
## Problem

During block-batch (initial) sync, `areDataColumnsAvailable` waits
**indefinitely** for a block's custody data columns — its `slotEnd` case
only logs and then keeps waiting; the only exits are "enough columns
arrived" or `ctx.Done()`. Because round-robin imports batches
**sequentially**, a single block whose columns are momentarily
unavailable blocks the whole import pipeline forever and sync
**dead-ends at a batch boundary** (no further blocks imported, no
error). For a near-tip block whose slot has already passed, `slotEnd` is
never even armed, so it stalls silently with no log.

## Fix

Bound the wait to **one slot**, scoped to the **sync/batch path only**
(`areSidecarsAvailable`, reached from `onBlockBatch`). On timeout the
batch returns an error and is retried by round-robin, which re-fetches
the columns — turning a hard dead-end into a recoverable retry. The
head/gossip and execution-payload-envelope DA paths (`process_block.go`
head check and `receive_execution_payload_envelope.go`) call
`areDataColumnsAvailable` directly and are intentionally left unchanged.

## Testing

- `go build ./beacon-chain/blockchain/`, `go test -tags develop
./beacon-chain/blockchain/ -run TestStore_OnBlockBatch` pass.
- Validated on **glamsterdam-devnet-5**: before the change a local
Prysm+Nethermind node repeatedly dead-ended at a batch boundary near the
tip; with this change the node syncs through and reaches head.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

author: terence
subject: Double the global per peer rpc rate limit (#16780)
body:
#### Summary

The `rpcLimiterTopic` collector caps total RPC requests per peer across
all topics combined. Every incoming req/resp message hits this limiter
in addition to its per-protocol cap. The current 5 req/s, burst 10 was
set when Prysm's rate limiter was first introduced and never revisited,
it is the strictest global per-peer cap in the ecosystem across all the
clients. This PR doubles it to 10 req/s, burst 20. Per-protocol limits

  #### Why
In practice a peer's normal sync traffic, status + ping + metadata + a
couple of range requests in the same second, easily exceeds 10 requests,
even before considering bursty block-by-range or envelope-by-range
traffic. The result is constant `ErrRateLimited` responses to spec
compliant peers

The cap was unjustifiably tight relative to the rest of the
implementations:
  | client | global per-peer cap | per-protocol notes |
  |---|---|---|
| Lighthouse | **none** (per-protocol only) | BlocksByRange: 128 tokens
/ 10s |
| Lodestar | **none** (per-protocol only, design copied from Lighthouse)
| BlocksByRange: `MAX_REQUEST_BLOCKS_DENEB` / 10s |
| Nimbus | ~8 req/s sustained, 40 burst (single global bucket) | no
separate per-protocol limits |
| **Prysm (today)** | **5 req/s, burst 10** | per-protocol limits also
enforced |
| **Prysm (after the pr)** | **10 req/s, burst 20** | per-protocol
limits also enforced |

  Doubling keeps the cap conservative but still stricter than Nimbus

author: Potuz
subject: Don't request data columns for empty slots in initial sync (#16976)
body:
In Gloas the column-fetch decision keyed off
block.Body().BlobKzgCommitments(), which returns the bid's committed
commitments (the builder's promise). For a payload-absent slot the
payload (and its data columns) is never revealed, so the node requested
columns that no peer can serve, looped on respondedSidecars=0, and never
synced past the slot.

Drive the decision off the revealed execution payload envelopes instead:
- Fetch payloads before sidecars so the envelope set is available.
- Select columns per revealed payload via columnFetchBlocks: Gloas
blocks only when an envelope exists for the block root; pre-Gloas (Fulu)
blocks always (payload is in the block). Request the out-of-batch
payload the first block builds on by its beacon block root (loaded from
the DB) and persist those columns via the queue consumer.
- Gate the import-side availability check (areSidecarsAvailable) on
payload presence so payload-absent Gloas blocks don't poll for
nonexistent columns.

---------

author: terence
subject: Dedupe Gloas pending-column downscore to once per peer per root (#17032)
body:
Under blob load a Gloas data column can be queued before its block
arrives. If the block is still missing when the pending entry is pruned,
every queued column's forwarder is downscored once per column. A single
peer that relayed many columns for one block then takes up to 128 hits
and instantly blows past the bad responses threshold of 5. That
disconnects an otherwise healthy peer, and under sustained load it
cascades into losing most peers. This change downscores each forwarder
at most once per orphaned root.

author: Preston Van Loon
subject: Fix unbounded growth of engine_exchangeCapabilities requested method list (#17004)
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

> Bug fix

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

`ExchangeCapabilities` appends the fork-specific engine endpoints
(Electra/Fulu/Gloas) to the **package-level** `supportedEngineEndpoints`
slice on every invocation:

```go
if params.FuluEnabled() {
    supportedEngineEndpoints = append(supportedEngineEndpoints, fuluEngineEndpoints...)
}
```

`ExchangeCapabilities` is called from `pollConnectionStatus` on every
execution-client (re)connection, and `pollConnectionStatus` is
re-invoked from the run loop on every failed `eth1HeadTicker` header
fetch (and via `retryExecutionClientConnection` from several error
paths). Each call therefore re-appends the fork endpoints to the shared
slice, so the slice grows without bound.

Because the requested-but-unsupported set is then computed from that
ever-growing slice, the resulting warning grows on every reconnect:

```
WARN execution: Connected execution client does not support some requested engine methods
  methods=[engine_getBlobsV3 engine_getBlobsV3 engine_getBlobsV3 ... (hundreds)]
```

This is most visible on execution clients that don't yet implement
`engine_getBlobsV3`/`engine_getBlobsV2`, and on nodes that reconnect to
the EL frequently.

The fix builds a fresh local endpoint list on each call instead of
mutating the shared package-level slice. The set of requested engine
methods is now stable across calls, so the warning is constant-length
(and duplicate-free) rather than monotonically growing. The shared
`supportedEngineEndpoints` slice is left read-only.

**Other notes for review**

Testing plan: added `Test_ExchangeCapabilities_StableAcrossCalls`, which
enables all forks, captures the engine-method list the EL receives via a
stub HTTP handler, calls `ExchangeCapabilities` twice, and asserts the
two requested method lists are identical and contain no duplicates. The
test fails on the previous code (`22` methods on the first call, `32` on
the second) and passes with this change. The full
`//beacon-chain/execution:go_default_test` package passes.

This change only affects the request list sent to the EL and the warning
log; it does not change which capabilities are cached or how they are
used. The warning will still appear once per reconnect when the EL
genuinely lacks a requested method — it simply no longer accumulates.

author: Alleysira
subject: Fix/addtrustedpeer empty addrs panic (#16757)
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

Bug fix


**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

`AddTrustedPeer` parses a peer multiaddr and then indexes
`info.Addrs[0]` without checking whether any transport address was
present. A peer-only multiaddr such as `/p2p/<peer_id>` can parse
successfully while producing an `AddrInfo` with an empty `Addrs` slice.
The unchecked index then panics. The same pattern also exists in
`connectWithAllTrustedPeers`.

This PR fixes this by:
- Added a length check after parsing the address in `AddTrustedPeer`.
- Skipped peers that have no dialable address before indexing `Addrs[0]`
in `connectWithAllTrustedPeers` and `peerIdsFromMultiAddrs`.
- Added `TestAddTrustedPeer_NoTransportAddress` to verify the handler
returns `400 Bad Request` instead of panicking.

**Which issue(s) does this PR fix?**

None.

subject: Remove Bazel: Phase 1/9 (#16986)
body:
**What type of PR is this?**
Other

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**
This pull request implements the **Phase 1** of:
- https://github.com/OffchainLabs/prysm/issues/16982

After this PR: proto, SSZ and mock files are generated without using
Bazel with `make gen`.

```
Prysm - Ethereum consensus client

Commands:
  make gen [proto ssz mocks]   Create generated code (default: all)
  make help                    Show this help
```

**Main difference with the Bazel world:**
In the Bazel world, for generated files differing between the minimal
and the mainnet configuration, only the mainnet code was actually
generated in the codebase, and Bazel used to re-generate on the flight
the minimal code.

Starting at this PR, both minimal and mainnet code are generated.

For these corresponding source files:
- `//go:build !minimal` is added in the header of the **mainnet** file
- Corresponding `.minimal.ssz.go` and `.minimal.proto.go` files are
created and `//go:build minimal` is added in the header of the
**minimal** file.

(Files that do not differ between the minimal an mainnet configuration
remain untouched.)

Please read commit by commit with the commit message.

subject: Check if Bazel generated `.pb.go` and `.ssz.go` would have outputed (almost) the same result. (#17056)
body:
**What type of PR is this?**
Other

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**
In
- https://github.com/OffchainLabs/prysm/pull/16986

we ensured that `make gen` would create almost the same output compared
to the former `hack` scripts.
I say "almost" here because the commented code in the header of the file
may differ.

We ensured that fact **for the state of the repository when the PR was
merged**.
However, it is possible that an eventual regression breaks this
assumption.

This pull request adds a new `hack/check-bazel-drift.sh` file.

This file:
1. runs the legacy proto hack script,
2. runs the legacy SSZ hack script,
3. ensures that only the `//go:build !minimal` and `protoc version` in
the header can differ. If there is any other differences, it returns on
error.

Also, this PR run this file in the CI with
`.github/workflows/check-generated-go.yml`

subject: Add forkchoice unit test (#16932)
body:
This PR adds a unit test as a regression test to prove @nflaig wrong :)

The test checks that even in the absence of attestations, if the

author: terence
subject: Ignore unverifiable execution payload bids on gossip instead of rejecting (#17044)
body:
The execution payload bid gossip validator rejected and penalized the
sender whenever the bid did not verify against the current head state,
which on glamsterdam-devnet-6 drove Prysm into a gossip score death
spiral and off the canonical chain. It now ignores rather than rejects
any bid whose parent block root is neither the current head nor the
proposer head, and logs the ignored case at debug.

author: terence
subject: Queue payload attestations received before the beacon block (#16909)
body:
PTC attestations gossiped before the node has the referenced beacon
block were dropped (ValidationIgnore), instead of being held and
processed once the block arrived. This pr adds a bounded pending queue
for those attestations, mirroring the existing pending payload-envelope
queue.

- Queue an attestation whose beacon_block_root is not yet in forkchoice,
keyed by block root.
- At queue time, verify committee membership and signature against the
current head state. The head state is not authoritative for the missing
block's branch, so a committee miss, or a committee the head state
cannot compute, is ignored and dropped rather than rejected, which
avoids penalizing peers. An invalid signature is still rejected, since
the validator key is authoritative once the index is confirmed in the
head PTC. Only attestations that pass both checks are queued.
- Request the missing block by root.
- Drain when the block is processed (both the gossip block subscriber
and the pending-blocks queue), re-checking the block-slot match, then
process and re-broadcast.
- Stale entries pruned every slot.

<!-- Thanks for sending a PR! Before submitting:

1. If this is your first PR, check out our contribution guide here

You will then need to sign our Contributor License Agreement (CLA),

4. Note that PRs updating dependencies and new Go versions are not

**What type of PR is this?**


> Bug fix


**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

This PR updates `async.Debounce` to return when its input events channel
is closed.

Previously, receiving from a closed channel produced the zero value
immediately. That could keep the debounce loop alive and eventually call
the handler with a zero-value event instead of exiting. The fix checks
the receive `ok` value in both event receive paths and returns when the
channel is closed.

A regression test was added to cover the closed-channel case and verify
that the handler is not called.

subject: Fix attestation ideal rewards for Electra balances (#17076)
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

Bug fix

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

Fixes the attestation rewards API `ideal_rewards` response for Electra
compounding validators with effective balances above 32 ETH.

Previously, `idealAttRewards` only generated rows for hard-coded 17–32
ETH effective balance buckets. Electra compounding validators can have

effective-balance buckets from the requested validators and sort them

author: terence
subject: Gate partial column decode on subscription to protect the gossip loop (#17074)
body:
`onIncomingRPC` runs on the shared pubsub `processLoop` and SSZ decodes
the attacker sized `PartialMessage` (up to ~8MB) before the subscription
check, so a peer can force multi-MB decodes on the loop that also
carries blocks and attestations, including for subnets we do not
custody.

How an attacker triggers it against a node running
`--partial-data-columns`:
1. Connect and negotiate the partial messages extension.
2. Send a `PartialMessagesExtension` RPC with `TopicID`
`data_column_sidecar_37` (a subnet the victim does not custody), a 33
byte `GroupID`, and a `PartialMessage` padded to roughly 4096 cells of
2048 bytes of garbage cells that are never KZG verified.
3. Stream these in a loop, reusing a few already established group IDs
so the library per group cap does not reject them

author: Potuz
subject: Drain pending Gloas data columns for our own proposed block (#17059)
body:
Our own proposed block is imported via the RPC path (ProposeBeaconBlock
-> ReceiveBlock) and never re-enters the gossip/by-root ingest paths
that drain pending Gloas columns. Columns peers reconstruct and gossip
back to us arrive before our local import, get queued as "block not yet
seen", and are never drained -- so the payload's data columns are
declared unavailable at slot end.

Subscribe sync to the statefeed BlockProcessed event (which fires on
every import path, including our own block) and drain the pending Gloas
columns for the processed root. Gated on regular sync to avoid needless
work on the initial-sync batch path.

subject: VC logging: Consolidate verbose logging messages after submitting messages for duties (#17083)
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

> Feature

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

Currently, we have verbose logs on `INFO` level after submitting the
following messages:
- sync message (`"Submitted new sync message"`)
- sync contribution and proof (`"Submitted new sync contribution and
proof"`)
- payload attestation message (only applicable for post-Gloas)
(`"Submitted new payload attestation"`)

This is pretty redundant especially when 1) we are running a devnet with
small count of nodes and 2) node operators are running VC with a lot of
validator keys.

This PR DO NOT remove those loggings; rather this downgrades those
logging to `DEBUG` level. And mirroring what we're doing on
attestations, VC collects the submitted message, emit multiple
"aggrgated" logs and then flush. Indices (e.g., validator, committee,
etc) are prettified with existing `PrettySlice`.

author: Jun Song
subject: VC logging: Correctly populate attestation data as a key (#17081)
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

> Bug fix

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

Right now, `FromAttData` will always return zeroed bytearray as it
populates attestation data in local copy. Fix this by chaning method
signature; receive pointer instead of value.

**Which issue(s) does this PR fix?**

N/A

**Other notes for review**

Regression test(`TestFromAttData`) is added.

Concrete example:

Say we have this log:
```
[2026-07-03 05:57:51.05]  INFO client: Submitted new attestations blockRoot=0x8da144cec21e committeeIndices=[0 0 0 0 0] pubkeys=[0xabc5b6a7b32b 0x989e1d295c19 0xafd9e7d88ddf 0xa7192e9f2fa7 0x86c30199be9e] slot=160 sourceEpoch=4 sourceRoot=0x39efba841543 targetEpoch=5 targetRoot=0x8da144cec21e
```

Under current code, `"Submitted new attestations"` will always show
**once**, as `submittedAtts` has one single entry keyed with zero bytes.
Different attestation data can sometime submitted by different
validators (e.g., BN fallback is activated during the slot), but this
wouldn't likely happen for same VC connected with same BN.

So this PR fixes a possible discrepancy where some of Prysm validators
submitted different attestation data (e.g., different
`beacon_block_root`) but the log only shows that overrided information
of attestation data. Suppose one validator submitted a vote for
`blockRoot=0x111122223333`, then the log will be emitted twice like:

```
[2026-07-03 05:57:51.05]  INFO client: Submitted new attestations blockRoot=0x8da144cec21e committeeIndices=[0 0 0 0] pubkeys=[0xabc5b6a7b32b 0x989e1d295c19 0xafd9e7d88ddf 0xa7192e9f2fa7] slot=160 sourceEpoch=4 sourceRoot=0x39efba841543 targetEpoch=5 targetRoot=0x8da144cec21e
[2026-07-03 05:57:51.05]  INFO client: Submitted new attestations blockRoot=0x111122223333 committeeIndices=[0] pubkeys=[0x86c30199be9e] slot=160 sourceEpoch=4 sourceRoot=0x39efba841543 targetEpoch=5 targetRoot=0x8da144cec21e
```

author: Jun Song
subject: Drop loopclosure static analyzer: can report false positives after Go 1.22 (#17108)
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

> Other

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

Drops loopclosure analyzer. As the [package
description](https://pkg.go.dev/golang.org/x/tools/go/analysis/passes/loopclosure)
says, this analyzer can report this code snippet as incorrect:

```go
for _, v := range list {
    defer func() {
        use(v) // incorrect
    }()
}
```

But since Go 1.22, this issue is resolved, which means if we declare a
variable via `:=`, its lifetime is independent of other loop iteration.

Originally included in #16999 when upgrading `x/tools` version, but I
think it's better to separate this PR.

**Which issue(s) does this PR fix?**

author: terence
subject: Skip nil builder entries in builderInsertionIndex (#17096)
body:
`builderInsertionIndex` dereferenced builder registry entries
unconditionally, but the slice can hold nil via gap-filling and hdiff. A
nil entry is now treated as a reusable slot, matching how the spec loop
handles a zero-value builder

author: terence
subject: Compute validator mid-slot delay from SLOT_DURATION_MS (#17098)
body:
Compute the validator client's mid-slot submission delay (proposer
preferences and builder preferences) from `SlotDuration()` instead of
`SECONDS_PER_SLOT`, so a config that sets only `SLOT_DURATION_MS` can't
turn the half-slot delay into a full slot and push every submission past
the slot deadline

author: terence
subject: Ignore signature failures for queued envelopes and payload attestations (#17103)
body:
- Queued payload envelopes and payload attestations reference a block we
have not seen yet, so their signatures are verified against the head
state, which may be on a different branch or behind on builder
registrations
- Rejecting on such failures downscores honest peers based on state we
cannot know is right, the same failure class as the devnet-6 bid
prev_randao incident, so return IGNORE instead
- Queue admission still requires a passing signature check, only the
peer penalty is dropped

author: terence
subject: Surface undefined engine errors from gloas forkchoice updates (#17094)
body:
Code health change, no real bug here. `notifyForkchoiceUpdateGloas`
logged undefined execution engine errors and returned a nil payload ID,
which callers treated the same as not proposing. It now returns error,
while callers keep their log-and-continue behavior.

author: terence
subject: Copy payload attestations out of the pool to prevent in-place aggregation races (#17099)
body:
- `PendingPayloadAttestations` returned live pool pointers while
`InsertPayloadAttestation` mutates the same entries' `Signature` and
`AggregationBits` in place under the pool lock, so a proposer
serializing the aggregate at slot start could observe a torn
signature/bits pair from a late PTC message and build an invalid block
- Return deep copies under the lock instead

author: terence
subject: Apply fork choice PTC votes for REST-submitted payload attestations (#17100)
body:
- The REST `POST /eth/v1/beacon/pool/payload_attestations` handler only
inserted into the pool and broadcast; unlike the gRPC path it never
called `ReceivePayloadAttestationMessage`, and self-published gossip is
not looped back, so a REST-connected VC's own PTC votes never reached
this node's fork choice
- Wire `PayloadAttestationReceiver` into the beacon REST server, apply
the fork choice vote after broadcast, and use `PtcLookupState` for the
committee index instead of the head state
- Enforce the same current-slot check the gRPC path has

author: terence
subject: Order Gloas before Fulu in gossip block topic mapping (#17114)
body:
- `GossipTopicMappings` checked `FuluForkEpoch` before `GloasForkEpoch`
in the block topic cascade; since any gloas epoch is also past fulu, it
returned `SignedBeaconBlockFulu` for gloas epochs and the gloas branch
was unreachable
- No impact today: the gossip decode path derives the block type from
the fork digest via `types.BlockMap` and only nil-checks this function's
result, so nothing consumes the wrong answer, but any future caller
trusting the epoch cascade would decode gloas blocks as fulu
- The existing test masked this by configuring gloas before fulu; the
test now uses the real fork order and asserts the block type at both
epochs, failing against the old branch order

author: terence
subject: Hold the state lock in QueueBuilderPaymentForSlot (#17095)
body:
`QueueBuilderPaymentForSlot` read `b.slot` and
`b.latestExecutionPayloadBid` without holding the state lock. It now
locks up front and dispatches to lock-free helpers, and both builder
pending withdrawal appends share the existing copy-on-write path

subject: Refactor validator client and REST package for better readability (#17091)
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

> Other

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

This PR includes several refactors that makes VC and REST provider much
simpler. I found it is bit hard to consume validator client package as
we use interface a lot, so I believe this PR will bring slight but
better readability.

Read commit by commit:

-
https://github.com/OffchainLabs/prysm/pull/17091/changes/7a2fb7a91140da6ca876b4b5c8f984c31dbbb571:
`NodeConnection` doesn't have to be an interface; harmful for code
readbility as well. For testing purpose, we can inject mock provider
either for REST or for gRPC.
-
https://github.com/OffchainLabs/prysm/pull/17091/changes/69dbd3f06bba8c4cba18636aae1df2981781bb38:
We uses interfaces a lot - removing unnecessary (de)referring
interfaces.
-
https://github.com/OffchainLabs/prysm/pull/17091/commits/ef4296d386573a707ccf57287b81ac377d018e5e:
Remove standalone factory packages. Maintaining dedicated package for
factory funtion only is not beneficial in terms of readability and
package dependency.
-
https://github.com/OffchainLabs/prysm/pull/17091/changes/82a46c6decd99389169ca54d0fa8ec34181d5766:
Remove obsolete `PrysmChainClient`. We already have `ChainClient` which
has richer interfaces. I couldn't find any reason to leave
`PrysmChainClient` as it is, we don't have a concrete plan for 1) adding
Prysm-specific endpoints and 2) use it in VC. In fact, when calling
`ValidatorPerformance` via `PrysmChainClient`, it literally checks
whether BN is Prysm or not. So I think this is an unnecessary
abstraction.
-
https://github.com/OffchainLabs/prysm/pull/17091/commits/7b469973416bf0a2506c108ec4b0efd196f5776e:
Simplifying `RestConnectionProvider`. Separate fields like `timeout` as
a config. Do not expose `HttpClient` as it won't be used.
-
https://github.com/OffchainLabs/prysm/pull/17091/changes/34bb62edb45cccaf6ad03b7b36eff48e16607708:
When client creation in factory, check whether REST provider is present,
and then pass the provider itself to factory function. It is interesting
that we ALWAYS check when VC startup whether REST is present or not
(mostly for event stream) so in production path REST provider shouldn't
be nil.

author: Preston Van Loon
subject: e2e: Reliability improvements (#16948)
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

Bug fix

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

This fixes a group of issues that were making
`//testing/endtoend:presubmit` unreliable. The goal is to fix the actual
harness/evaluator issues instead of marking the target flaky.

The main changes are:

1. Make e2e evaluators wait for stable state instead of failing on
transient reads. This includes head convergence checks, deterministic
eth1 vote expectations, Fulu participation decoding, and a narrow
startup skip for sync participation through slot 3. Slot 4 and later are
still checked.

2. Fix eth1 transaction generation under fork and txpool pressure. Blob
tx generation is now fork-aware, sender nonce/gas price state is tracked
across iterations, blob modes use separate funded accounts across the
Fulu boundary, and local geth is started with `--rpc.txfeecap=0`.

3. Use `HeadETH1Data()` instead of random eth1data when
`BlockByTimestamp(latestValidTime)` fails. Random eth1data is still used
for the disconnected case, but short EL lag should not introduce
avoidable nondeterminism.

4. Fix harness false negatives. Checkpoint sync now waits for matching
heads instead of a specific log string. Doppelganger detection reads the
existing validator log instead of truncating it, uses the direct wait
result, and the log scanner can handle long lines.

**Which issues(s) does this PR fix?**

Fixes #

**Other notes for review**

Testing:

- `//testing/endtoend/evaluators:go_default_test`
- `//testing/endtoend/components/eth1:go_default_test`
- `//beacon-chain/rpc/prysm/v1alpha1/validator:go_default_test`
- `//testing/endtoend:presubmit`
- `//testing/endtoend:presubmit --runs_per_test=10`

The runs_per_test=10 was sufficient evidence that the changes were a
significant improvement, but Buildkite found one more CI-only startup
case at epoch 0 slot 3 in `validator_sync_participation_0`. The final
boundary fix keeps that skip limited to startup and keeps slot 4+
enforced.

subject: Remove Bazel: Phase 2/9 (#17007)
body:
**What type of PR is this?**
Other

Please read commit by commit.

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

This pull request implements the **Phase 2** of:
- https://github.com/OffchainLabs/prysm/issues/16982

This PR has 3 commits excluding the changelog commit:

### 1. Add a cache to `make gen`.
Running `make gen` will generate the `.gen-cache.json` file:
```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "kinds": {
    "mocks": "078ff63a6c068fb125f404b558df6dd4e4e44d671c6422940e725c2776d7889d",
    "proto": "50fd4f18a3620da10fdb65351f5beb879b06ce7b18ff8b1f73b2643457a9131c",
    "ssz": "dcfdb25339fd94d04523b837c48982a07ab705b4074386b3e7a8a0eae8944235"
  }
}
```

Running `make gen` a second time if everything is up to date will be
instant.

The `make gen` help is now:
```
Commands:
  ...
  make gen [proto ssz mocks] [mode=force|no-force]   Create generated code (default: all,no-force)
  ...
```

To force re-generation, the user can either remove the `.gen-cache.json`
file, or use
```
make gen mode=force
```

### 2. Implement `make build`
Running
```
make build <binary>
```
will:


1. call `make gen`
2. call `go build -o "dist/<binary>" ./cmd/<binary>`

The `make build` corresponding help is:
```
Commands:
  ...
  make build [<bin>...] [flags=...]                  Build a binary (default: all)
  ...

Options:
  <bin>:           beacon-chain client-stats prysmctl validator
```

Calling `make build` (no parameter) will build all the binaries listed
in the help.

### 3. Implement `make run`
Running
```
make run <binary>
```
will:

1. call `make gen`
2. call `go run ./cmd/<binary/>`

The `make run` corresponding help is:
```
Commands:
  ...
   make run <bin> [flags=...] [-- <args>]             Run a binary
  ...

Options:
  <bin>:           beacon-chain client-stats prysmctl validator

Notes:
  After '--', pass '--flag value' (not '--flag=value')
```

author: terence
subject: Validate and cache published execution payload bids before broadcast (#17101)
body:
- The bid publish endpoints (REST `PublishSignedExecutionPayloadBid` and
gRPC `SubmitSignedExecutionPayloadBid`) only broadcast: the subscriber
pipeline skips self-published gossip and peers never echo a message back
to its origin, so a bid submitted directly to the proposer's BN never
entered that node's highest-bid cache and self-build always won
- Verify the bid against the gossip rules (parent state, builder
active/version/balance, preferences fee recipient and gas limit, prev
randao, signature) before broadcasting, so the node doesn't relay bids
peers would reject and downscore it for
- Record the verified bid in the local highest-bid cache and emit the
operation feed event from the shared gRPC path; the REST handler now
delegates to it

**What type of PR is this?**

> Uncomment one line below and remove others.
>
> Bug fix


**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

This PR updates `scrapeProm` to propagate the final error returned by
`prom2json.FetchMetricFamilies`.

`FetchMetricFamilies` closes the metric-family channel before returning
some scrape errors, such as non-200 HTTP responses. The previous select
loop could observe the closed channel first and return a successful
result with a nil error, hiding the actual scrape failure.

The fix always forwards the final fetch result on `errChan` and waits
for it when the metric-family channel closes. A regression test covers
the non-200 response case.

body:

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

`POST /eth/v1/beacon/rewards/attestations/{epoch}` returns an error
response like:

This is because it calculates HTR of block root with
`latest_block_header`. This PR guarantees that calculting HTR cannot be
wrong as it ALWAYS lives in the DB, finding ancestor of the block, so

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

`getPort` returned `(0, true)` for an ENR whose `tcp`/`udp`/`quic` entry
is present but set to `0`. `retrieveMultiAddrsFromNode` then built an
undialable `/ip4/x/tcp/0` (or `/udp/0/quic-v1`) multiaddr, which is
stored in the peerstore and dialed — a guaranteed-failing connection
attempt. This treats a zero port as absent so such peers are skipped,
matching how a missing entry is already handled (and how other clients,
e.g. go-ethereum's dialer, behave).

Found during a cross-client discv5 audit.

**Other notes for review**

Regression test added in `beacon-chain/p2p/discovery_test.go` (fails
before, passes after). Changelog fragment included.

author: james-prysm
subject: making proposer preferences repush on reconnection to different node (#17066)
body:
**What type of PR is this?**
 Bug fix


**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

proposer preferences has a feature to deduplicate sends as it checks
each slot , but if the validator disconnects from a beacon node it won't
send to the new beacon node as a fresh push because of the local
deduplication.

this pr adds a counter instead of pure host comparisons so that it
adresses reconnection to the same node, along with a check if we did
reconnect to a new bn and force pushes the pr. this issue was found
while reviewing https://github.com/OffchainLabs/prysm/pull/17063

**note**: this has not been applied to builder preferences yet so
something similar should be reviewed there.

## Testing

Verifies that when the VC fails over to a different beacon node
**without** the runner restarting (health never flips), the connection
counter still forces a re-push so the new node receives our proposer
preferences. This is the path the health-recovery force cannot cover.

**1. Build validator + beacon images** from this branch and tag them for
Kurtosis:
`gcr.io/offchainlabs/prysm/validator:latest` and
`gcr.io/offchainlabs/prysm/beacon-chain:latest`.

**2. Launch a post-Gloas devnet where one VC has a 2-beacon fallback
list.** Save as `gloas-fallback-test.yml`:

```yaml
participants:
  # TARGET VC: primary cl-1, fallback cl-2
  - el_type: ethrex
    el_image: ethpandaops/ethrex:glamsterdam-devnet-5
    cl_type: prysm
    cl_image: gcr.io/offchainlabs/prysm/beacon-chain:latest
    vc_image: gcr.io/offchainlabs/prysm/validator:latest
    vc_extra_params:
      - --verbosity=debug
      - --beacon-rpc-provider=cl-1-prysm-ethrex:4000,cl-2-prysm-ethrex:4000
    count: 1
  # backdrop: keeps the chain healthy, provides cl-2..cl-4
  - el_type: ethrex
    el_image: ethpandaops/ethrex:glamsterdam-devnet-5
    cl_type: prysm
    cl_image: gcr.io/offchainlabs/prysm/beacon-chain:latest
    vc_image: gcr.io/offchainlabs/prysm/validator:latest
    vc_extra_params: [--verbosity=debug]
    count: 3
network_params:
  fulu_fork_epoch: 0
  gloas_fork_epoch: 1
  seconds_per_slot: 6
  genesis_delay: 30
global_log_level: debug
```

```
kurtosis run github.com/ethpandaops/ethereum-package --args-file gloas-fallback-test.yml --enclave gloas-fallback
```

**3. Verify the fallback list took effect** (the package sets its own
`--beacon-rpc-provider`; ours is appended and wins):

```
cid=$(docker ps --filter name=vc-1-ethrex-prysm -q)
docker logs "$cid" 2>&1 | grep "Initialized gRPC connection provider"
# expect: count=2 endpoints=[cl-1-prysm-ethrex:4000 cl-2-prysm-ethrex:4000]
```

**4. Wait for Gloas** (head slot >= 32) and confirm steady state
(`prefsBuilt=0` on quiet slots):

```
docker logs "$cid" 2>&1 | sed -E 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*m//g' | grep "Build proposer preferences result" | tail
```

> Use `docker logs`, not `kurtosis service logs` — the latter only
returns ~200 lines (startup).

**5. Kill the primary beacon during a quiet mid-epoch slot** (not
epoch-start, not mid-epoch, so the re-push is unambiguous):

```
kurtosis service stop gloas-fallback cl-1-prysm-ethrex
```

**6. Observe** in the target VC log:

```
docker logs "$cid" 2>&1 | sed -E 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*m//g' \
  | grep -iE "Switched (gRPC endpoint|to responsive)|Build proposer preferences result|unhealthy|Starting validator runner"
```

**Expected (PASS):**
- `Switched gRPC endpoint newHost=cl-2... previousHost=cl-1...` and
`Switched to responsive beacon node`.
- **No** `Beacon node unhealthy, stopping runner` and **no** new
`Starting validator runner` — health did not flip and the runner did not
restart, so this exercises the connection-counter path (not the restart
path).
- The next `Build proposer preferences result` on a normally-quiet slot
shows `alreadySubmitted` dropping (cache cleared) and **`prefsBuilt` >
0** (the re-push), followed by a `SubmitSignedProposerPreferences` RPC
to cl-2.

**FAIL (regression):** after the switch `prefsBuilt` stays `0` — the new
beacon never receives the preferences.

**Cleanup:**

```
kurtosis enclave rm -f gloas-fallback
```

<details><summary>Observed run (2026-07-01)</summary>

Killed `cl-1-prysm-ethrex` at 14:58:26, chain slot ~250 (epoch 7, quiet
window):

```
slot 250-254 (pre-kill):  prefsBuilt=0  alreadySubmitted=12      # steady state
14:58:40  Switched gRPC endpoint             newHost=cl-2  previousHost=cl-1
14:58:40  Switched to responsive beacon node current=cl-2  previous=cl-1  tried=[cl-1]
slot 255 (14:58:45):      prefsBuilt=6  alreadySubmitted=6       # cache cleared + re-push
14:58:48  gRPC SubmitSignedProposerPreferences -> cl-2           # re-push on the wire
```

No `unhealthy` / `stopping runner`; only the original `Starting
validator runner` (14:32:30). Slot 255 is off-cadence (not epoch start,
not mid-epoch); in steady state it was `0`. The 12->6 `alreadySubmitted`
drop is `submittedPrefSlots` being cleared by `forceFullPush`, and
`prefsBuilt=6` is the re-push to cl-2.

</details>


**Which issue(s) does this PR fix?**

Fixes #

author: Chase Wright
subject: Return an error for an invalid --p2p-local-ip (#17117)
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

Bug fix

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

In `buildOptions`, when `--p2p-local-ip` is set but not parseable, the
code returned `errors.Wrapf(err, "invalid local ip provided: ...")` —
but `err` at that point is the already-checked (nil) result from the
preceding `MultiAddressBuilder` call. `errors.Wrapf(nil, ...)` returns
`nil`, so `buildOptions` returned `(nil, nil)` and silently ignored the
misconfiguration, starting the node with default options instead. Use
`errors.Errorf` so the invalid value surfaces.

Found during a cross-client discv5 audit.

subject: Skip data columns of empty slots in by range RPC handler (#17089)
body:
The data column sidecars by range handler served stored columns for
every canonical block, including slots whose payload never became
canonical, and peers reject those as unrequested roots. Column serving
now follows the canonical payload chain using the same successor and bid
comparison rule as the envelopes by range handler, and columns of the
undecided chain tip are served only once the envelope has been
processed.

subject: Fix flaky pending attestation bucket tests (#17154)
body:
- These tests assert exact entry counts on a global logrus hook, which
captures logs from every goroutine in the test binary. Background
goroutines left running by other sync tests (libp2p hosts, gossipsub)
occasionally emit a log line during the assertion window, making the

bucketAttestationsByData tests.

author: terence
subject: Reset self-build envelope signature failure budget every slot (#17104)
body:
`selfBuildSigFailures` limits how many signature verifications we spend
on self-build envelopes that arrive before their block, but it is a
lifetime counter with a reset that almost never fires. The reset lives
in `prunePendingPayloadEnvelopes` and only runs when the prune deletes
an entry older than the finalized epoch, which requires a queued
envelope whose block never arrived to sit in the map for 2+ epochs. On a
healthy chain every queued envelope drains within seconds when its block
arrives, so nothing survives to be pruned and the counter only counts
up.

The counter can grow on honest traffic: queued envelopes are verified
against the head state's proposer lookahead, so a valid envelope
arriving at an epoch boundary while the head state is still in the
previous epoch fails the check and increments it. Once it reaches 3, the
limit check runs before signature verification, so every future
self-build envelope that beats its block over gossip is dropped without
being checked or queued, permanently. Example:

- epoch boundary, head state one epoch behind, valid self-build envelope
arrives before its block, signature verified against the wrong
lookahead, counter goes 1
- this repeats at two later boundaries over days of uptime, counter
reaches 3
- from then on every self-build envelope that arrives before its block
is ignored at the cap check, the payload is only recovered by the
by-root fetch a slot later, and this node's PTC votes payload absent in
the meantime

Scope the failure budget to the current slot instead: the queue only
admits current-slot envelopes, so the counter now resets whenever the
slot advances, keeping the DoS bound (3 wasted signature checks per
slot) while making the worst case self-heal at the next slot boundary.
The prune-path reset is removed.

author: terence
subject: Mark full node gas limit (#17093)
body:
Full nodes created by `MarkFullNode` and `InsertChain` had no gas limit,
so after a restart or batch sync `ForkChoice.GasLimit` returned 0 for
the head and bid gossip validation ignored every real bid until the next
envelope import. Both paths now take the gas limit from the block's bid,
and `insertFirstPayloadIfNeeded` reads it from the parent block

author: terence
subject: Fail block data column availability check during initial sync instead of blocking (#17152)
body:
- During initial sync, `isDataAvailable` waits on
`areDataColumnsAvailable` with no bound. For a block whose slot has
already passed, the slot-end timer is never armed, so if the block's
custody columns are missing the init-sync consumer blocks forever and
sync silently dead-ends. #16978 bounded the batch path and #16994 fixed
the payload envelope path, but checkpoint sync routes every block
through this per-block path (`syncToNonFinalizedEpoch` -> `ReceiveBlock`
with nil `avs`).
- Example from a stuck mainnet checkpoint sync
(https://gist.github.com/nalepae/345a926d7ac0d3335de07d612d99a0d3), the
node imports a few blocks then stops with no error and never recovers:

```
[13:21:32.39]  INFO blockchain: Synced new block block=0x614562f4... slot=14738725
[13:21:32.41]  INFO blockchain: Called new payload with optimistic block ... slot=14738726
(nothing after this, block processing never resumes)
```

- Fix mirrors #16994: during initial sync, check column availability
synchronously with `dataColumnsAvailableNow` and return an error if
columns are missing, so round robin retries the batch and refetches the
columns instead of hanging.
- Added a regression test that stalls forever without this change.

author: terence
subject: Bound Gloas data column sidecar slot before queueing (#17157)
body:
Fixes #17149. Gloas data column sidecars are unsigned, so an attacker
controls their slot. The unseen-block path queued them without a slot
check, letting a far-future slot create a pending entry that pruning
never evicts, permanently exhausting the queue with ~8 messages.

This ignores future-slot sidecars before they reach the pending queue,
so every queued entry is prunable within a slot. The gloas spec dropped
the future-slot and above-finalized gossip conditions along with the
signed header, so this is client-side hardening, not a spec condition.

author: Potuz
subject: wait for clock on da (#17168)
body: Fixes a flaky test mostly

author: terence
subject: Apply Gloas state-diff pending deposits against pre-upgrade list (#17158)
body:
Fixes #17147. At the Fulu to Gloas fork, upgrade onboarding removes
builder deposits from pending_deposits, but the state-diff index is
computed against the raw Fulu anchor while apply time ran the upgrade
first and then indexed the now-shortened list, panicking with slice
bounds out of range or silently corrupting the queue on nodes running
`--enable-state-diff`.

This captures the anchor's pending_deposits before the version upgrade
and applies the diff against that list, with a bounds check as a
backstop.

author: terence
subject: Re-verify builder deposit signatures when in-batch index reuse evicts a pubkey (#17111)
body:
- Batch pre-verification classifies deposits as new-builder vs top-up
against the pre-batch state, but an in-batch index reuse can evict a
pubkey, so a request classified as top-up can actually register a new
builder with an unchecked signature
- Re-verify the signature at apply time when the request was not batch
pre-verified
- Add tests for both eviction outcomes, invalid signature skipped and
valid signature re-registered

author: terence
subject: Stop downscoring peers when pruning pending Gloas data columns (#17170)
body:
- Pruning the pending Gloas column queue no longer downscores forwarding
peers, `!HasBlock(root)` only means this node has not imported the block
yet
- Under ordinary lag every peer forwards columns for the same unimported
canonical root, so the penalty banned the entire peer set against a
threshold of 5 and the node self-isolated to 0 peers with a stalled EL
- Verification failure downscores in `processPendingGloasColumns` are
unchanged
- Fixes #17166

author: james-prysm
subject: Fix event stream reconnect (#17120)
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

Bug fix

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**
Follow-up to https://github.com/OffchainLabs/prysm/pull/17066: while
testing
that PR's failover behavior on a Kurtosis devnet I noticed the event
stream never rebinds after
a host switch — `Received head_v2 event` stops permanently until the VC
restarts. The gap
pre-dates #17066 (the stream was only ever started once, at runner
startup), but #17066's
seamless-failover path is what made it visible, so this closes the
remaining piece: after a
failover the new beacon node now gets the proposer preferences *and* the
event stream

- `StartEventStream` becomes `EnsureEventStream`, called on every slot
tick from the runner. It reconciles the stream with the current
connection: starts it if it isn't running, replaces it if the beacon
connection generation changed since it was bound (using the
`connTracker` from #17066 with a new `event-stream` kind), and is a
no-op otherwise.
- New `event.StreamGuard` guarantees at most one stream feeds the events
channel: replacing a stream cancels the previous run and waits for it to
exit before the successor starts. This covers the degraded-host case
where the old host's stream is still alive after the switch.
- `EventStream.Subscribe` no longer closes the caller-owned events
channel on context cancel (the channel is reused by the replacement
stream), and all channel sends are now cancellation-aware so a replaced
stream can't deadlock on a full channel.
- `ConnectionGeneration` moves onto the validator client interface so
the tracker reads the counter of whichever transport (gRPC/REST) is
actually active.

**1. Build validator + beacon images** from this branch and tag them
`gcr.io/offchainlabs/prysm/validator:latest` /
`gcr.io/offchainlabs/prysm/beacon-chain:latest`.

**2. Launch a post-Gloas devnet where one VC has a two-beacon fallback
list.** The target VC runs in REST mode with a 2-host REST list *plus* a
present-but-idle 2-host gRPC list (the r3511683129 scenario:
`ConnectionGeneration` must read the active transport's counter, not the
non-nil idle one). Three backdrop nodes keep consensus healthy and
provide the fallback target. Save as `gloas-fallback-test.yml`:

```yaml
participants:
  # TARGET: primary beacon cl-1, fallback cl-2. This is the VC we fail over.
  - el_type: ethrex
    el_image: ethpandaops/ethrex:glamsterdam-devnet-5
    el_extra_params:
      - --http.api=eth,net,web3,admin
    cl_type: prysm
    cl_image: gcr.io/offchainlabs/prysm/beacon-chain:latest
    vc_image: gcr.io/offchainlabs/prysm/validator:latest
    supernode: true
    cl_extra_params:
      - --verbosity=debug
    vc_extra_params:
      - --verbosity=debug
      - --beacon-rpc-provider=cl-1-prysm-ethrex:4000,cl-2-prysm-ethrex:4000
      - --enable-beacon-rest-api
      - --beacon-rest-api-provider=http://cl-1-prysm-ethrex:3500,http://cl-2-prysm-ethrex:3500
    count: 1
  # BACKDROP: keeps consensus healthy and provides cl-2/cl-3/cl-4.
  - el_type: ethrex
    el_image: ethpandaops/ethrex:glamsterdam-devnet-5
    el_extra_params:
      - --http.api=eth,net,web3,admin
    cl_type: prysm
    cl_image: gcr.io/offchainlabs/prysm/beacon-chain:latest
    vc_image: gcr.io/offchainlabs/prysm/validator:latest
    supernode: true
    cl_extra_params:
      - --verbosity=debug
    vc_extra_params:
      - --verbosity=debug
    count: 3

network_params:
  fulu_fork_epoch: 0
  gloas_fork_epoch: 1

```

**3. Verify the target VC came up in the bug scenario** — REST mode with
BOTH providers initialized (our `vc_extra_params` are appended after the
package's own flags and urfave/cli takes the last):

```

# INFO grpc: Initialized gRPC connection provider count=2 endpoints=[cl-1-prysm-ethrex:4000 cl-2-prysm-ethrex:4000]

```

> Use `docker logs`, not `kurtosis service logs` — the latter returns
only ~200 startup lines.

**4. Wait for Gloas** (head slot ≥ 32; with 6s slots that's ~3.5 min
after genesis) and confirm steady state: `Received head_v2 event`
flowing ~1/slot, and `Build proposer preferences result` showing
`prefsBuilt=0` with a stable `alreadySubmitted` on quiet slots:

```

curl -s "http://127.0.0.1:$port/eth/v1/beacon/headers/head" | grep -o '"slot":"[0-9]*"'
docker logs "$cid" 2>&1 | sed -E 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*m//g' | grep -cE "Received head_v2 event"
```

**5. Kill the primary beacon in a quiet slot** (mid-epoch, away from the
epoch-start/mid-epoch push points, so the forced re-push is
unambiguous):

```
kurtosis service stop gloas-fallback cl-1-prysm-ethrex
```

**6. Observe the failover + rebind** (~1–2 health-check intervals after
the kill):

```
docker logs --since 3m "$cid" 2>&1 | sed -E 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*m//g' \
  | grep -E "Switched|Starting event stream|Event stream|Confirmed push|re-push after beacon connection change|Submitted proposer preferences|unhealthy|Starting validator runner"
```

**Expected (PASS):**
- `Event stream interrupted ... unexpected EOF` (old stream dies with
cl-1), then `Switched to responsive beacon node current=...cl-2...`.
- `Confirmed push for new beacon connection kind=event-stream` +
`Starting event stream reason=stream not running topics=[head_v2
execution_payload_available]` — the rebind.
- `Received head_v2 event` resumes within a few slots and keeps flowing
~1/slot from cl-2.
- **No** `Beacon node unhealthy, stopping runner`, **no** new `Starting
validator runner` — health never flipped; this is the
connection-generation path, not the restart path. Exactly 2 `Starting
event stream` in the whole log (boot + rebind).
- The #17066 re-push bracket shares the same slot tick undisturbed:
`Forcing proposer preferences re-push` → `Submitted proposer
preferences` → `Confirmed ... kind=proposer-preferences`, with
receiver-side proof on cl-2: `Processed signed proposer preferences`.

author: Jun Song
subject: Fail payload reconstruction in Gloas if reconstruction correctness cannot be guaranteed (#17174)
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

> Bug fix

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

Reported in Discord ([Message
link](https://discord.com/channels/595666850260713488/892088344438255616/1526470317315457165)).


https://github.com/OffchainLabs/prysm/blob/73439ebe08e6cee85e5e9dbc24ac60dd71d4294d/beacon-chain/execution/engine_client.go#L182-L196

Today, Prysm reconstructs the series of execution payload envelopes from
multiple sources:
1. DB: Saves (and read) *blinded* payload envelope which deliberately
omits large-sized transactions, withdrawals, and **BAL**.
2. Call Engine API (`engine_getPayloadBodiesByHashV2`) for getting
payloads. Note that this can return `null` `blockAccessList` when BAL
has been pruned from storage. (ref:
https://github.com/ethereum/execution-apis/blob/main/src/engine/amsterdam.md#engine_getpayloadbodiesbyhashv2)
3. Call Engine API (`eth_getBlockByHash`) for getting execution blocks.

So it is possible to construct a payload with empty BAL, when the
envelope originally had non-empty BAL at that slot. The problem is that
we uses the signature from the DB, which can be deviated as the message
becomes different. (non-empty BAL -> empty BAL)

This PR returns an error when reconstruction cannot guarantee the
correctness, which means:
- if EL cannot provide execution payloads or
- length of BAL is zero - BAL shouldn't be zero-byted in terms of RLP.

**Which issue(s) does this PR fix?**

N/A but should solve the issue in `glamsterdam-devnet-6`. ([Discord
link](https://discord.com/channels/595666850260713488/892088344438255616/1526470317315457165)))

**Other notes for review**

~~`TestReconstructExecutionPayloadEnvelope_BlindedStorage` covers
possible scenarios that I can think of.~~

author: james-prysm
subject: properly switches to v2 proposer duties post gloas (#17171)
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

Feature

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**
The REST-mode validator client now requests proposer duties from
`/eth/v2/validator/duties/proposer/{epoch}` for epochs at or after the
Gloas fork, and keeps `/eth/v1/...` before it. Follow-up to the
discussion in #17036
(https://github.com/OffchainLabs/prysm/pull/17036#discussion_r3569690796).

Post-Gloas, the split duties path detects mid-fetch reorgs by comparing
the next-epoch proposer dependent root against the next-epoch attester
dependent root (`depRootsDiverged`), falling back to a full refetch on
mismatch. That comparison is written against the fork-aware (EIP-7917)
dependent-root semantics, which only v2 guarantees. The gRPC client
already uses `GetProposerDutiesV2`; the REST client was still hard-coded
to v1.

The pre-Gloas combined-duties path stores the proposer dependent root as
`CurrDependentRoot` and matches it against head events'
`current_duty_dependent_root` (block root at `epoch_start − 1`) —
exactly v1's semantics. Switching that path to v2 would break the
head-event comparison on post-Fulu networks, so the endpoint choice is
gated at Gloas, matching where the split path (the only consumer of the
fork-aware comparison) activates.

## How to test with Kurtosis

**1. Build local images from this branch:**

```bash
bazel build //cmd/beacon-chain:oci_image_tarball --platforms=@io_bazel_rules_go//go/toolchain:linux_arm64_cgo --config=release
docker load -i bazel-bin/cmd/beacon-chain/oci_image_tarball/tarball.tar
bazel build //cmd/validator:oci_image_tarball --platforms=@io_bazel_rules_go//go/toolchain:linux_arm64_cgo --config=release
docker load -i bazel-bin/cmd/validator/oci_image_tarball/tarball.tar
```

(Use `linux_amd64_cgo` on x86 hosts. Loads as
`gcr.io/offchainlabs/prysm/{beacon-chain,validator}:latest`.)

**2. Network config** (`gloas.yml`) — the key parts are
`--enable-beacon-rest-api` on the VC (this PR only affects REST mode;
without it the VC uses gRPC and never hits the changed code) and Gloas
activating after genesis:

```yaml
participants:
  - el_type: ethrex
    el_image: ethpandaops/ethrex:glamsterdam-devnet-5
    cl_type: prysm
    cl_image: gcr.io/offchainlabs/prysm/beacon-chain:latest
    vc_image: gcr.io/offchainlabs/prysm/validator:latest
    supernode: true
    vc_extra_params:
      - --verbosity=debug
      - --enable-beacon-rest-api
    count: 4
network_params:
  fulu_fork_epoch: 0
  gloas_fork_epoch: 1
  seconds_per_slot: 6
additional_services:
  - dora
```

```bash
kurtosis run github.com/ethpandaops/ethereum-package --args-file gloas.yml --enclave gloas-rest
```

**3. What to check** (from epoch 2, ~8 min after genesis; VC container
names are `vc-N-ethrex-prysm--*`):

```bash
docker logs <vc-container> 2>&1 | grep -E 'Promoting|diverg|Updated duties'
```

Expected:

- `Promoting cached next-epoch duties to current` once per epoch from
epoch 2 onward.
- **No** `Proposer and attester dependent roots diverged` warnings.
- **No** `Updated duties due to ... dependent root change` churn
(head-event comparison stays consistent).

**Which issue(s) does this PR fix?**

Fixes #

author: Jie Ma
subject: Fix nil block dereference in Gloas envelope/data-column gossip validation (#17184)
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

Bug fix

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

tldr: a seen block can still be `nil` in DB.

The Gloas gossip validators for execution payload envelopes and data
column sidecars fetch the referenced block with `beaconDB.Block(ctx,
root)` and then call `block.Block()` without a nil check. The preceding
`chain.HasBlock` gate can report a block as seen while it still lives
only in the init-sync cache and hasn't been flushed to the DB, in that
case beaconDB.Block returns `(nil, nil)`, and the dereference panics.

This PR: 
- adds a nil guard after the block fetch (Ignore if nil), following
guard already used in
[here](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/prysm/blob/88ef96684ec080e4e728c85feca7bed8272504c7/beacon-chain/sync/rpc_beacon_blocks_by_root.go#L226).
- includes regression tests for both cases.

Without this PR, both new regression tests fail, panic with a
nil-pointer dereference.

**Which issue(s) does this PR fix?**

None.

**Other notes for review**

Wonder if Ignore is the right result for a nil block? I kept the minimal
guard here.

Thanks!

author: Potuz
subject: Do not queue blocks that arrive more than 500ms early (#17167)
body:
Starting in https://github.com/OffchainLabs/prysm/pull/8975 Prysm added
blocks to the pending queue when they arrived even up to 24 seconds into
the future. This unnecessarily opens a DOS window for free on the node.

In addition, the node performs an HTR before checking if it's from the
future.

This PR removes entirely the pending queue path for these future blocks
and just ignores any block that arrives earlier than the 500ms into the
slot. Also moves up the check for this earlier than performing the HTR.

h/t to the EF protocol security team for pointing out the issue fixed in
this PR.

subject: fix(ci): restore coverage runfiles and fail fast (#17189)
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

Bug fix

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

The Buildkite Bazel configuration disables runfile links globally, but
the coverage report generator is a local action that needs its runfiles
symlink forest. As a result, passing Go tests can still fail during
coverage report post-processing because the generator cannot locate its
runfiles.

This PR enables `--build_runfile_links` specifically for the `coverage`
command while leaving the build default unchanged. It also adds `set
-euo pipefail` to the coverage script so Bazel or analysis failures
propagate to Buildkite instead of being masked.

subject: fix(e2e): serialize fixed-port postsubmit targets (#17190)

**What type of PR is this?**

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

The `go_builder_test` and `go_minimal_postmerge_test` E2E targets both
derive service ports only from the Bazel shard index. Bazel can schedule
same-index shards from these targets concurrently, causing both
processes to bind the same ports and fail nondeterministically.

This PR tags both fixed-port targets as `exclusive`, preventing Bazel
from overlapping them while preserving their existing two-way sharding.

author: Preston Van Loon
subject: fix(validator): synchronize remote web3signer key file watcher startup (#17188)
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

Bug fix

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

Fixes two issues in the remote web3signer keymanager that affect
validators
running with `--validators-external-signer-key-file`.

1. **Startup race.** `NewKeymanager` launched the key-file watcher in a
background goroutine and returned immediately. Validator startup then
raced
watcher initialization: early key lookups could observe an empty or
stale
   key set before the watcher performed its initial read, and a watcher
   initialization failure was only logged, never surfaced to the caller.
`NewKeymanager` now blocks until the watcher signals readiness through a
buffered channel guarded by `sync.Once`, and returns an error if the
watcher
   fails to initialize. `refreshRemoteKeysFromFileChanges` threads a
`markReady` callback that fires once the file is registered and the
initial
   key load completes.

2. **Lock-ordering deadlock.** `updatePublicKeys` called
   `accountsChangedFeed.Send` while holding the keymanager write lock.
`Feed.Send` blocks until every subscriber receives, and subscribers
re-enter
the keymanager under the read lock (e.g. `FetchValidatingPublicKeys`),
so the
send could deadlock against the held write lock. The lock is now
released
before the send, and the debug log reads the local slice instead of the
   shared field.

Tests now wait on an account-change subscription instead of sleeping on
the
watcher, removing a fixed one-second sleep and a flaky post-write
assertion.

**Which issue(s) does this PR fix?**

N/A — small bug fix (no tracking issue).

**Other notes for review**

- Behavioral change: `NewKeymanager` now returns an error when the file
watcher cannot initialize (previously logged and continued), and blocks
  briefly until the watcher is ready.
- Testing plan: `bazel test
//validator/keymanager/remote-web3signer:go_default_test`.

author: Manu NALEPA
subject: Remove Bazel: Phase 3/9 - Part 1 (#17062)
body:
**What type of PR is this?**
Other

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

This pull request implements the first part of **Phase 3** of:
- https://github.com/OffchainLabs/prysm/issues/16982

> [!NOTE]
> Phase 3 covers both unit tests and end to end tests. However this pull
request is already big enough, so we chose to split Phase 3 in 2 parts:
unit tests (this one), and then end to end tests (to be implemented).

This pull requests implements `make test`, and `make testdata`.

Main design changes:
- Bazel supports flaky tests. This is not the case for `go test`. To
support flaky tests, we use
[gotestsum](https://github.com/gotestyourself/gotestsum) as a test
harness.
- Some tests (eg: spectests), require to fetch external data. This was
handled by Bazel. This PR handles this as well.

`make test` runs tests. External data are lazily fetched directly into
the tests, and are cached.
With this PR, all unit tests (even the ones than previously used to
depend on Bazel) can be ran with `go test` directly. This also means
that those tests can be run with a classical go debugger in an IDE.

`make testdata` only fetches the test data. This is **not** a
requirement before running `make test`. It's only a convenience tool if
human eyes on the test data are needed.


> [!IMPORTANT]
>  **Main difference with Bazel tests:**
> Bazel tests support retrying panicking tests. This is not the case for
[gotestsum](https://github.com/gotestyourself/gotestsum).
> Because of that, this PR starts by some commits fixing panicking
tests, or converting panicking tests to erroring tests.

If needed, we probably can do some extra work to support panicking tests
as well, but I think it's not a bad thing not to support panicking
tests.

This PR also runs `make test` in the CI as **info only**. A failing
`make test` won't fail the whole CI.

The `Makefile` has been updated as:
```
Prysm - Ethereum consensus client

Commands:
  make run <bin> [flags=...] [-- <args>]       Run a binary
  make build [<bin>...] [flags=...]            Build a binary (default: all)
  make gen [<kind>...] [mode=force|no-force]   Create generated code (default: all,no-force)
  make test [<kind>...] [mode=no-race|race]    Run unit tests (default: all,no-race)
  make testdata                                Pre-fetch external spec-test data
  make clean                                   Clean everything
  make help                                    Show this help

Options:
  <bin>:         beacon-chain client-stats prysmctl validator
  gen <kind>:    proto ssz mocks
  test <kind>:   mainnet mainnet-spectest minimal minimal-spectest

Notes:
  After '--', pass '--flag value' (not '--flag=value')
```

author: james-prysm
subject: improve logs when not actually exiting just protducing the exit files (#17177)
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

Bug fix


**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

`validator accounts voluntary-exit --exit-json-output-dir` writes signed
exit files to disk and never broadcasts them — but every prompt and log
in that flow used the same wording as a real broadcast exit. A user was
asked to confirm "a voluntary exit", and on completion was told
**"Voluntary exit was successful for the accounts listed"** with
beaconcha.in URLs to "track each validator's exit" — even though no exit
was submitted and the validators remain fully active. Anyone taking that
message at face value could believe their validators were exiting when
nothing had been sent to the network.

With this change, when `--exit-json-output-dir` is set:

- The confirmation prompts say what will actually happen: *"write a
signed voluntary exit file (the exit will NOT be broadcast)"* /
*"continue writing signed voluntary exit files? No exits will be
broadcast to the network."*
- The final message reports files written instead of a successful exit:
*"Signed voluntary exit files were written to `<dir>`. No exits were
broadcast to the network. The validators listed will NOT exit until
these files are submitted to a beacon node."*

Behavior without the flag is unchanged (verified below), and no exit
logic changed — only prompt/log text. Also fixes a typo in an error
message ("validator exist json" → "validator exit json").

Local testing

```bash
docker exec -i $(docker ps --filter name=vc-1-ethrex-prysm -q) sh -c \
  'echo y | /validator accounts voluntary-exit --accept-terms-of-use \
    --wallet-dir=/validator-keys/prysm \
    --wallet-password-file=/prysm-password/prysm-password.txt \
    --beacon-rpc-provider=cl-1-prysm-ethrex:4000 \
    --exit-all --exit-json-output-dir=/tmp/exits'
```

Observed output (the new wording):


```
About to write signed voluntary exit files (no exits will be broadcast) for 128 accounts
===============CONFIRMATION NEEDED===============
continue writing signed voluntary exit files? No exits will be broadcast to the network. (y/n):
...
INFO accounts: Wrote signed validator exit JSON to /tmp/exits/validator-exit-127.json
INFO accounts: Signed voluntary exit files were written to /tmp/exits. No exits were broadcast
to the network. The validators listed will NOT exit until these files are submitted to a beacon
node. pubkeys=0xaaf6c1251e73, ...
```

All 128 `validator-exit-<index>.json` files were written with valid
`message`/`signature` contents.

**Verified nothing was broadcast:**

```bash
curl -s $CL/eth/v1/beacon/pool/voluntary_exits           # → {"data":[]}
curl -s $CL/eth/v1/beacon/states/head/validators/0       # → active_ongoing, exit_epoch 18446744073709551615
```

**Control — behavior without the flag is unchanged.** Same command
without `--exit-json-output-dir` (answered `n` to abort) shows the
original broadcast wording:

```
About to perform a voluntary exit of 128 accounts
===============CONFIRMATION NEEDED===============
continue with the voluntary exit? (y/n):
```

**Which issue(s) does this PR fix?**

Fixes # https://github.com/OffchainLabs/prysm/issues/17161

author: Preston Van Loon
subject: fix(e2e): make voluntary-exit selection deterministic (#17200)
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

Bug fix

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

The voluntary-exit evaluator previously used `rand.Intn` to pick a
validator, which made test runs non-deterministic and could silently
skip the exit scenario when all selected candidates happened to be in
the upcoming sync committee with no fallback.

This PR makes selection deterministic and bounded:

- Eligible validators are iterated in index order so every run picks the
same candidate given the same state.
- Validators outside the upcoming sync committee are preferred. When
every eligible validator is in the committee, the evaluator falls back
to those reserved candidates rather than skipping the scenario entirely.
- If no exit is successfully submitted after both the
execution-credential path and the selected-candidate path run, the
evaluator now returns an explicit `no eligible validators available for
voluntary exit` error instead of silently succeeding.
- The `rand` import is removed from the evaluator.

**Which issue(s) does this PR fix?**

N/A

**Other notes for review**

Testing performed:

- Evaluator selector unit tests ran three times uncached (verbose Bazel)
and once with `-race` and randomized test order; all passed.
- Minimal e2e voluntary-exit chain passed: proposal, exited,
withdrawal-submission, and withdrawn evaluators all green.
- Mainnet-style exit chain passed in all three attempts for the
voluntary-exit proposal, exited, and withdrawal-submission evaluators.
- The mainnet parent target was nonzero across all three runs solely
because the unrelated `blobs_included_in_blocks_epoch_13` evaluator
reported no blobs in epoch 12. This PR does not claim a fully green
mainnet parent target.
- `make build` and `gopls`/Gazelle checks passed.
- The zero-submission guard is covered by a table-driven test that
checks the explicit error and the one- and two-submission success cases.

author: Tristan-Wilson
subject: Fix makeslice panic in blob versioned-hash filtering for duplicate commitments (#17199)
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

Bug fix

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

`GET /eth/v1/beacon/blobs/{block_id}?versioned_hashes=<vh>` panics with
`runtime error: makeslice: cap out of range` when a requested versioned
hash
matches a KZG commitment that appears more than once in the target block
(legal per consensus rules — e.g. mainnet slot 8626186 carries the same
commitment three times). net/http recovers the panic per-request, so the
node
survives, but every such request aborts with a connection reset and a
panic
stack in the logs. Remotely triggerable on any node whose block DB
contains a
duplicate-commitment block: hash matching runs before any blob-storage
access, so blob pruning does not prevent it.

Root cause, in `resolveBlobsContext`
(`beacon-chain/rpc/lookup/blocker.go`):
requested hashes are deduplicated into a set, but `indices` receives one
entry per *matching commitment*. The missing-hash detection then
compares
raw counts:

    if len(indices) != len(cfg.VersionedHashes) {
missingHashes := make([]string, 0,
len(cfg.VersionedHashes)-len(indices)) // negative cap → panic

One requested hash matching N≥2 duplicate commitments makes the capacity
negative. The same count heuristic causes two more defects:

- A client repeating a hash in the query gets a spurious 404 with an
empty
`missing:` list, even though the hash is in the block (the handler does
not
  deduplicate query values).
- Duplicate matches can make the counts line up and mask a genuinely
missing
hash: requesting `[vh(A), vh(B)]` against a block with commitments `[A,
A]`
  returns 200 with both copies of A and no B.

The fix accounts for found/missing hashes on unique hash sets: the
request
fails iff some unique requested hash matched no commitment.
Duplicate-matching
commitments still contribute one index per occurrence, since sidecars
are
position-indexed objects, and the existing block-order filter semantics
are
preserved. Error message wording is unchanged; its counts now refer to
unique
hashes.

**Which issue(s) does this PR fix?**

None filed (small bug fix per the contribution guidelines).

**Other notes for review**

- Introduced by #15610 (`7e32bbc199`); reproduced against v7.1.7.
- The deprecated `/eth/v1/beacon/blob_sidecars/{block_id}` endpoint is
not
  affected (it only parses `indices`), but the internal
  `BlobSidecars`/`resolveBlobsContext` lookup path accepts
  `WithVersionedHashes` and is fixed for all callers.

**Testing plan**

New regression test `TestResolveBlobsContext_DuplicateCommitments`
exercises
the conversion directly (no storage needed — the panic precedes storage
access). Against the unfixed code, the first subtest reproduces the
exact
`makeslice: cap out of range` panic, and the spurious-404 /
masked-missing-hash
subtests fail. `go test ./beacon-chain/rpc/lookup/
./beacon-chain/rpc/eth/blob/`
passes.

Live repro (any node serving a block with duplicated commitments):
`curl
"$NODE/eth/v1/beacon/blobs/8626186?versioned_hashes=0x01c7011435804298c2e816d32e51791eacf8921494a317d54f029a4d4b9823a7"`

author: Manu NALEPA
subject: `saveHead`: Clear the head cache when the head is updated. (#17143)
body:
**What type of PR is this?**
Bug fix

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**
When `GetAttestationData` is called (for example by a validator client
via the
/[eth/v1/validator/attestation_data](https://ethereum.github.io/beacon-APIs/#/Validator/produceAttestationData)
endpoint for the slot `n` while the block at slot `n` is not yet
imported, then the attestation data corresponding to the current head
(most of the time, corresponding to the block at slot `n-1`) is returned
by the beacon node.

However, if, after the block corresponding to the slot `n` is imported,
`GetAttestationData` is called again for the slot `n`, this function
**still returns the attestation corresponding to the previous head**.

Why? Because, during the first `GetAttestationData` call, the
attestation data is cached for slot `n`, and all eventual calls (even if
the head actually changed after the first call) will return the cached,
stalled attestation data.

While this is a real bug, most of the time this is not really an issue,
because the validator clients will call `GetAttestationData` only after
they received the corresponding `head` SSE event from the beacon node,
showing that the head is effectively updated.

However, in an `active-active` configuration this is an issue:

```
VC-1 --\
        + ----> BN-1
       /
VC-2 -+
       \
        ------> BN-2
```

1. VC-2 is connected in an `active-active` mode to both BN-1 and BN-2.
VC-1 is only connected to BN-1.
2. BN-2 imports the block at slot `n` (**not** BN-1), and emits the
`head` event.
3. VC-2 calls `GetAttestationData` to both BN-1 and BN-2.
4. BN-2 responds with respond with the block at slot `n`, BN-1 with the
block at slot `n-1`. VC-2 keeps the response of BN-2. (VC-1, only
connected to BN-1, does not do anything at this time.)
5. BN-1 finally imports the block at slot `n`, and emits the `head`
event.
6. VC-1 calls `GetAttestationData` to BN-1 only.
7. Because of the present cache issue, `BN-1` still responds to with the
attestation data corresponding to the slot `n-1`, **even if the block at
slot `n` is now imported.**
8. VC-1 votes for the stalled head, missing the head reward (and,
potentially, the source and the target reward if this issue happens at
the beginning of the epoch).

This PR fixes this issue by clearing the head cache when the head is
updated.

author: james-prysm
subject: making duties failures independent of each other (#17036)
body:
**What type of PR is this?**
 Feature


**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**


#16421 split validator-client duty fetching across gRPC/REST and
introduced **promotion** — instead of re-pulling both current and next
epoch every boundary, the cached next-epoch duties are promoted into the
current epoch and only the new next-epoch is fetched.

This PR finishes the two follow-ups #16928 left open:

1. **Next-epoch duties are always optional.** Previously a next-epoch
*attester* fetch failure was a hard error that aborted the whole update
— disrupting the *current* epoch too. Now every next-epoch duty type
fails softly (flagged, not fatal), so a next-epoch problem never breaks
the current epoch.
2. **Failures are retried per-type, not bundled.** Previously any single
missing next-epoch duty forced a full re-pull of *all four* duty types
at the next boundary. Now the missing types are re-fetched
**individually, mid-epoch**, and merged in — so promotion stays cheap
and a single transient failure doesn't cascade.

A third, related change keeps the dependent-root (reorg) handling
consistent with the new soft-failure model.

## What changed

### Next-epoch duties optional
`missingNextDuties` gains a `missingNextAttester` bit. In both the
full-fetch and promotion paths, a failed next-epoch attester is logged
and flagged (not returned as an error), exactly like proposer/sync/ptc
already were. Current-epoch attester/proposer remain required.

### Per-type mid-epoch retry
- `RetryMissingNextDuties` re-fetches **only** the duty types flagged
missing and overlays them onto the existing next-epoch duties
(`overlayNextDuties`), leaving the types that already succeeded
untouched. If the **attester spine** itself is missing (the attester
assignment is what creates each validator's duty row, so without it
there are no rows to overlay onto), it rebuilds the whole next epoch
instead.
- `MaybeRetryMissingNextDuties` is what the run loop calls each
non-epoch-start slot. It runs the retry in its **own goroutine** so the
current slot's attestation/proposal isn't blocked, but only when there's
actually missing work (`needsNextRetry`) and no retry is already in
flight (`retryInFlight` CAS) — so we don't spawn goroutines for nothing
or pile them up.
- Writes are guarded by a store **revision** counter: if an
epoch-boundary or head-event update lands while a retry goroutine is
mid-fetch, the now-stale write is dropped (`replaceNextDuties` applies
only if the store is still at the revision the fetch was based on).

### Dependent-root / reorg handling
`checkDependentRoots` no longer treats an *unknown* (nil) current
dependent root as "needs update" — that state only arises after a soft
next-epoch attester failure, and forcing a full `UpdateDuties` on every
head event while it's nil is wasteful. Recovery is instead owned by the
epoch boundary and the per-slot retry. Current-epoch reorg detection
(the `prev` dependent-root path) is unchanged.

## Before / after

### Per-duty-type fetch failure

| Duty type | Current epoch fails | Next epoch fails — **before** | Next
epoch fails — **now** |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Attester** | hard error → keep cached duties, retry next tick |
**hard error → aborts the whole update, breaking the current epoch** |
soft: flag `missingNextAttester`; spine rebuilt by the mid-epoch retry |
| **Proposer** | hard error → keep cache | soft, but forced a full
4-type re-pull next boundary | soft: flag; overlaid by the mid-epoch
retry |
| **Sync** | soft (logged) | soft, forced a full 4-type re-pull | soft:
flag; overlaid by the mid-epoch retry |
| **PTC** | soft (logged) | soft, forced a full 4-type re-pull | soft:
flag; overlaid by the mid-epoch retry |

### Triggers → action

| Trigger | **Before** | **Now** |
|---|---|---|
| Epoch boundary, no failures + same validators + stable dep root |
promote next→current, fetch next epoch only | same |
| Epoch boundary, can't promote (first run / validator-set drift) | full
fetch (current + next, all types) | same |
| Epoch boundary, a next-epoch type failed last cycle | **forced full
re-pull of all 4 types** | **promote** — the gap was already filled
mid-epoch |
| Mid-epoch slot | *(nothing — wait for next boundary)* | **retry only
the missing next-epoch types**, in a goroutine off the slot critical
path; no-op when nothing is missing |
| Head event, dependent root changed | `UpdateDuties` | same |
| Head event, current dependent root **unknown (nil)** | **trigger
`UpdateDuties`** | **skip** — let the boundary + per-slot retry recover
|

**Which issue(s) does this PR fix?**

Fixes #https://github.com/OffchainLabs/prysm/issues/16928
