author: james-prysm
subject: grpc use execution_payload_available event (#17500)
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

Bug fix

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

gRPC validator clients never received `execution_payload_available` —
the gRPC event stream only
carried the head topic — so every PTC vote waited out the deadline:
4.51s into a 6s slot, versus
0.23s for a REST client on the same chain.

- New deprecated-tagged `StreamExecutionPayloadAvailable` RPC on
`BeaconNodeValidator` forwards the
existing `statefeed.ExecutionPayloadAvailable` event as `{slot,
block_root}` — the same signal the
REST SSE topic serves. A 16-deep outbox with its own sender goroutine
returns `ResourceExhausted`
  rather than letting a slow client stall envelope processing.
- The gRPC VC's `StartEventStream` runs it alongside `StreamSlots`,
emitting the same event JSON as
REST. `ProcessEvent` and the `payloadAvailability` waiter are unchanged.
- Against an older beacon node the stream returns `Unimplemented`; the
VC warns once per bind
(`Beacon node does not support payload availability streaming; gRPC PTC
votes will wait for the
deadline. Upgrade the beacon node or use --beacon-rest-api-provider for
on-arrival voting`) and
keeps deadline voting on the head stream. Any other stream failure tears
both down and the runner
  re-binds as before.
- Not changed: the REST path; head_v2 over gRPC still downgrades to v1
head (#13563).

# Follow-ups, deliberately separate

- **Deadline-path tolerance differs.** With no event, REST re-polls for
500ms past the due mark;
gRPC asks once. Only matters if the node's clock trails the VC's; zero
occurrences observed. The
right fix is server-side — `Service.PayloadAttestationData` waiting out
its own deadline instead
of returning `Unavailable` — which makes both transports identical with
no client code.
- **REST logged empty slots as errors**, dropping the node's `204`
during re-poll. Found in this run,
fixed on `ptc-no-content-classification`; not caused here. this pr try
to fix it https://github.com/OffchainLabs/prysm/pull/17510
- **`payloadAvailability` is pruned only on `notify`**, so a node that
never emits the event (the
  compat path above) grows it unbounded. Small standalone fix.


## How this was tested

4-node geth/prysm kurtosis devnet, gloas from genesis, 6s slots,
spamoor, slots 0–319, images
`Prysm/v7.1.8/d85408468c…`. The package forces Prysm VCs into REST mode,
so the gRPC VCs were
started by hand reusing the kurtosis volumes. Same VC binary everywhere:
`grpc-vc-1` → cl-1 (PR),
`vc-2`/`vc-3` REST → cl-2/cl-3 (PR), `grpc-vc-4` → cl-4 running develop
`7730c643fe` with no
`StreamExecutionPayloadAvailable` — the A/B control.

author: Potuz
subject: Cap self-built payload envelopes at one per valid proposer per slot (#17433)
body:
## Problem

In `queuePendingPayloadEnvelope`, both capacity caps
(`maxPendingPayloadRoots=128`, `maxPendingBuildersPerRoot=2`) are gated
behind `!isSelfBuild`, and all self-build envelopes share one
builder-index constant (`BuilderIndexSelfBuild`) so the per-root
`inner[builderIdx]` dedup never fires across roots.

A malicious current-slot proposer holds the proposer key and can sign an
unbounded number of self-build envelopes, each with a **different**
`beacon_block_root`, all validly signed. Each new root both adds a
pending-map entry and fires a `sendBatchRootRequest` goroutine to fetch
the unknown block. The resulting flood of spurious block-by-root
requests gets **us banned by our peers**.

## Fix

Cap self-build at **one queued payload per valid proposer index per
slot**, keyed on the head-state proposer for the current slot
(`helpers.BeaconProposerIndexAtSlot`). A valid self-build signature
already ties the envelope to exactly that proposer, so the key is
deterministic and not attacker-controlled.

- The seen-proposer entry is recorded **only after** a successful
signature verification, so a non-proposer peer cannot reserve or block
the real proposer's slot with a bad envelope.
- Keying per proposer (not globally per slot) still admits one payload
per **distinct valid proposer** in a forked scenario where the head
reorgs to a branch with a different slot proposer — bounded by our own
reorgs, not the attacker.
- The existing per-slot `maxSelfBuildSigFailures` budget is retained to
bound bad-signature floods from non-proposers.
- `queuePendingPayloadEnvelopeFromRootRequest` needs no change — it
already enforces the caps and never fires a root request.

## Tests

Added to `pending_payload_envelope_test.go`:
- **Flood** (one proposer, many distinct roots) → exactly one queued
payload.
- **Distinct fork proposers** (head reorg to a different valid slot
proposer) → two queued payloads.
- **Bad-sig-does-not-reserve** → a bad-signature envelope neither
reserves the proposer's slot nor blocks the subsequent valid one.

Pre-existing `SelfBuildBypasses*` tests still pass, confirming honest
self-build is never starved by the external-builder caps; the new
per-proposer bound is orthogonal.

author: Jun Song
subject: Marshal states directly behind their DB version key when saving (#17518)
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

> Other: Optimization

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

This PR uses `MarshalSSZTo` instead of `MarshalSSZ`, which requires one
more copy for the SSZ object. The size of buffer is expected as we have
`SizeSSZ` API, so it makes sense to set the capacity with this size
getter.

With this PR, state saving would be much more efficient, and it has a
high impact for the nodes with lower `slots-per-archive-point` (e.g.,
32). This can be a good memory optimization before we make hdiff in
production.

**Which issue(s) does this PR fix?**

N/A

author: satushh
subject: Serve the chain tip's envelope in envelopes by range when fork choice holds the tip full (#17533)
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

Feature

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

- The envelopes by range handler walks backwards from the successor
bid's ParentBlockHash, so when a request reached the chain tip the tip's
own envelope was never served: no descendant bid commits to its payload.
- When the successor lookup falls back to the head root, start the walk
from the tip bid's BlockHash if fork choice selects the tip's full
payload variant, per the PAYLOAD_STATUS_FULL head condition of
[consensus-specs#5608](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/5608).

years ago](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/prysm/releases/tag/v4.0.7).
And in our [documentation for
builder](https://prysm.offchainlabs.com/docs/configure-prysm/builder/#registration-cache),
it says:

> Validator registrations for Builder APIs are stored in a cache by
default as of 4.0.7 instead of bolt db when starting the beacon node.
... In the future the db used to store registrations will be removed
completely and the flag will no longer be required for this feature.
Validator settings will be persisted on the validator client side.

This PR in one line: Remove all legacy DB usage for builder service.
This requires to deprecate one flag: `--disable-registration-cache`. I
think it's worth doing at this moment because we're aheading Gloas which
requires significant change for proposer settings and by giving up this
niche flag code complexity and dependency graph gets much simpler.

**Which issue(s) does this PR fix?**

N/A

**Other notes for review**

Each commit incrementally applies the change.

- [Deprecate flag:
--disable-registration-cache](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/prysm/pull/17515/commits/148af46c7e6112ee9e96b401f19d4cdebfdf2829):
Move the flag into deprecated zone.
- [Remove the validator registration DB
path](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/prysm/pull/17515/commits/12510b8bb1670af4b415ec9f80dae65f896559b6):
`RegisterValidator` and `RegistrationByValidatorID` only checks the
registration cache which is our hot path at this point.
- [Read fee recipients from the proposer preferences
cache](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/prysm/pull/17515/commits/5634468c99ee0e29774b4edc920f00063e314c8b):
`GetFeeRecipientByPubKey` (which has no production caller in the
codebase but anyway) now checks the cache instead of calling
`BeaconDB.FeeRecipientByValidatorID`. Thus we now don't have any `Fee
recipients operations.` in our DB.

author: fmtappendf
subject: Fix --max-health-checks off-by-one (#17570)
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

Bug fix

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

`--max-health-checks=N` shut the validator down on the **N+1-th**
consecutive failed health check instead of the N-th. `updateStatus`
compared the counter before incrementing it, so `fails` first had to
reach `maxFails` and then take one more failed check to reach the
shutdown branch:

```go
} else if m.maxFails > 0 && m.fails < m.maxFails {
    m.fails++                                    // #1: 0 -> 1, #2: 1 -> 2, #3: 2 -> 3
} else if m.maxFails > 0 && m.fails >= m.maxFails {
    m.cancel()                                   // #4: 3 >= 3, shutdown
}
```

That contradicts the flag's own documentation, which describes a failure
count rather than "N retries after the first failure":

> Maximum number of consecutive failed health checks before exiting. A
health
> check fails when no connected beacon node is ready. Set to 0 or a
negative
> number for indefinite checks.

The changelog entries from #15401, which added the flag, read the same
way ("after the given number of health check failures").

This PR increments the counter first and then compares, so N failed
checks means N. The `maxFails <= 0` indefinite-retry path is untouched,
and the counter still resets on a healthy check, so the "consecutive"
part of the documentation stays accurate.



**Which issue(s) does this PR fix?**

Fixes #<issue number>

**Other notes for review**

The existing test encoded the off-by-one (`initialFails: 2` with
`maxFails: 2` expected the cancel on the third failure), so it is
corrected here along with two new table cases: `maxFails=1` cancelling
on the first failure, and one failure short of the limit staying alive.

New `TestHealthMonitor_CancelsOnMaxConsecutiveFails` probes step by step
for `maxFails` of 1, 2 and 3 and asserts the shutdown happens on exactly
the `maxFails`-th consecutive failure, plus a subtest covering that a
healthy check in between resets the count. Both fail on `develop` and
pass with this change; `go test ./validator/client/ -count=1` passes.

author: terence
subject: Accept late previous-fork attestations on the current fork's subnet topic (#17562)
body:
Unaggregated attestation topic validation derived the expected digest
from the attestation's slot, so after a fork boundary a late attestation
from the previous fork's epoch published on the current fork's topic was
rejected. The subscriber already ignores messages on non-current
digests, so the check now compares against the current fork digest,
matching the spec which only checks the subnet.

author: terence
subject: Reject Builder-API bids whose block hash equals the parent block hash (#17556)
body:
validateBuilderBid now enforces bid.block_hash != bid.parent_block_hash,
which process_execution_payload_bid and bid gossip already check, so a
builder can no longer make the proposer build an invalid block.

author: terence
subject: Apply block PTC votes to every seat and skip votes for older blocks (#17555)
body:
Block-carried payload attestations now write each voter's vote to every
PTC seat it holds, matching on_payload_attestation_message and the
gossip path. Votes whose data.slot does not match the voted block's slot
are skipped, as the spec returns early for them after a skipped slot.

author: terence
subject: Reject by-root Gloas column sidecars whose slot does not match the block (#17557)
body:
Gloas sidecars have no signed block header, so the by-root path accepted
any slot and stored the column under it, which could push the pruner
cutoff forward. The sidecar slot is now checked against the local
block's slot.

author: terence
subject: Reject PTC lookups for pre-Gloas slots at the fork epoch (#17531)
body:
The previous-epoch PTC window is all zeros at the fork, so validator 0
could produce valid payload attestations for pre-fork slots. Mirror
consensus-specs#5652 by rejecting get_ptc lookups before the fork epoch
while the state is on the Gloas fork version.

subject: Fix data race in proposer settings snapshot access (#17569)
body:
<!-- Thanks for sending a PR! Before submitting:

1. If this is your first PR, check out our contribution guide here
https://docs.prylabs.network/docs/contribute/contribution-guidelines
You will then need to sign our Contributor License Agreement (CLA),
which will show up as a comment from a bot in this pull request after
you open it. We cannot review code without a signed CLA.
2. Please file an associated tracking issue if this pull request is
non-trivial and requires context for our team to understand. All
features and most bug fixes should have
an associated issue with a design discussed and decided upon. Small bug
   fixes and documentation improvements don't need issues.
3. New features and bug fixes must have tests. Documentation may need to
be updated. If you're unsure what to update, send the PR, and we'll
discuss
   in review.
4. Note that PRs updating dependencies and new Go versions are not
accepted.
   Please file an issue instead.
5. A changelog entry is required for user facing issues.
-->

**What type of PR is this?**

> Uncomment one line below and remove others.
>
> Bug fix


**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

This PR synchronizes proposer settings snapshot publication and
retrieval.

`UpdateProposerSettings` already serializes clone-then-swap updates, but
`ProposerSettings` previously read the pointer without synchronization.
`Graffiti` also accessed the field directly. Runtime keymanager/API
updates could therefore race with validator slot processing.

This change:

- changes `proposerSettingsMu` to an `RWMutex`;
- protects snapshot retrieval with `RLock`;
- makes `Graffiti` retrieve one synchronized snapshot instead of
accessing the field directly;
- extends the concurrency regression test to exercise updates
concurrently with `ProposerSettings` and `Graffiti` reads.

The read lock only protects retrieval of the pointer. Continuing to read
the returned snapshot after releasing the lock is safe because updates
clone the settings and never mutate previously published snapshots.


**Which issue(s) does this PR fix?**

Fixes https://github.com/OffchainLabs/prysm/issues/17568

author: james-prysm
subject: adding builder settings flags for proposer settings (#17519)
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

Feature

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

Operators can now configure Gloas builders for all validators from the
command line, the way `--suggested-fee-recipient` sets the default fee
recipient, instead of needing a proposer settings file, URL, or
keymanager API call:

- `--builder-urls` — comma-separated builder URLs; auth data may be
appended as a hex fragment (`https://builder.example#0x0123`), otherwise
the URL's UTF-8 bytes are used.
- `--builder-min-bid`, `--builder-boost-factor`,
`--builder-max-execution-payment` — Gwei / percentage / Gwei, written
only when set so an explicit `0` stays distinct from "inherit".

How the flags behave, in three rules:

1. **The flags set the default builder settings for this run only.**
Pass them on every start, like `--enable-builder`. A start without them
clears any default builders list left in the DB by an earlier run and
warns once. Without `--suggested-fee-recipient`, the flags keep the
default fee recipient already in the DB.
2. **Everything else keeps its precedence.** A settings file or URL
`default_config` replaces the flag default and warns which flags it
overrode. Per-key settings from a file, URL, or the keymanager API win
over the flag default and are never touched.
3. **Before Gloas, a non-empty `--builder-urls` list turns builder
registration on**, the way `--enable-builder` does, for every key that
resolves a fee recipient. A per-key `builders: []` opts that key out.
`--enable-builder` behaves as before.
4. **`--suggested-gas-limit` now applies from Gloas onward too.** It
sets the default gas limit that pre-Gloas registrations and post-Gloas
proposer preferences both read, so after the fork it overrides the
network gas limit schedule (EIP-8261). Operators should remove it once
Gloas is live to follow the schedule. Startup warns when the flag is set
on a network with Gloas scheduled, and separately when the value exceeds
the highest scheduled gas limit; the existing per-epoch warning covers
the active schedule value. Like the builder defaults, the default gas
limit applies per run: a start without the flag drops the persisted one
and warns once.

Keys inherit from the flag default field by field: a key with only a fee
recipient uses the flag builders; a key with its own list keeps it and
inherits unset preferences such as `min_bid`. A run whose only default
content is builder flags persists nothing and no longer logs the
"proposer settings are empty" warning.

Schema handling: any builder flag stamps the flag source with the
highest supported schema version (`MaxSchemaVersion`, currently 2); an
unversioned file with v2 fields is still inferred as version 2. The
merge dispatches on `version < 2` for the legacy path, so later schema
versions take the current path by default. `--enable-builder` still
applies as legacy pre-Gloas content and is scrubbed at the Gloas cutover
as before; on version 1 databases `--suggested-gas-limit` also keeps
writing the legacy builder-level gas limit, which the cutover scrubs
while the option-level default carries over. On a network with no Gloas
fork scheduled the flags are accepted with a warning.

The help text of every defaults-only flag, `--suggested-fee-recipient`
included, now ends with "Per-key settings from a proposer settings file,
URL, or the keymanager API take precedence." The one new startup log is
a Warn that fires once when a restart drops a persisted default builders
list because neither builder flags nor a settings source configured one:

```
Dropped the default builder settings a previous run stored in the validator DB because neither builder flags nor a settings source configured a builders list this run; pass --builder-urls or the settings file on every start
```

Not changed: settings-file and keymanager behavior, the runtime
`EffectiveBuilderConfig` resolution, bid selection on the beacon node,
and the version 1 builder merge. The flagless behavior changes are the
version 2 switch rule above, which applies to a DB that an earlier run
already stamped version 2, and the per-run default gas limit in rule 4.

## How the flags work together

All six flags set the defaults for this start, the `default_config` of
the proposer settings. Per-key settings from a settings file, URL, or
the keymanager API always win over them. A file or URL `default_config`
replaces the flag defaults as a whole.

| Flag | Sets | Before Gloas | From Gloas | Restart without it |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--suggested-fee-recipient` | default fee recipient | fee recipient
for proposals and builder registrations | fee recipient in proposer
preferences | kept from the DB |
| `--suggested-gas-limit` | default gas limit | gas limit in builder
registrations, sent only while registration is on | gas limit in
proposer preferences for every key; overrides the network schedule,
remove it to follow the schedule | dropped, one warning |
| `--enable-builder` | legacy builder toggle | turns builder
registration on for keys with a fee recipient | no effect, warned,
cleared at the fork | dropped, as today |
| `--builder-urls` | default builders list | a non-empty list turns
registration on, like `--enable-builder` | builders to request bids from
| dropped, one warning |
| `--builder-min-bid` | default minimum bid | none | floor for builder
and gossip bids | dropped |
| `--builder-boost-factor` | default boost factor | none | weight of
bids against the local payload; 100 is neutral, 0 always builds locally
| dropped |
| `--builder-max-execution-payment` | default payment cap | none |
execution payment counted for bids from the listed builders | dropped |

| Combination | Result |
|---|---|
| `--builder-urls` with `--enable-builder` | Redundant before Gloas.
`--enable-builder` still logs its legacy warning. |
| `--builder-urls` without `--suggested-gas-limit` | Registrations and
preferences use the network default gas limit, or the schedule once one
is active. Nothing is carried over from an earlier start. |
| `--suggested-gas-limit` without `--enable-builder` or `--builder-urls`
| Before Gloas nothing sends it. From Gloas it is the preference gas
limit for every key. |
| `--builder-min-bid` or `--builder-boost-factor` without
`--builder-urls` | Still apply to gossip bids, and per-key builder lists
inherit them. |
| `--builder-max-execution-payment` without `--builder-urls` | No effect
until a builders list exists. Per-key lists inherit it. |
| Builder flags without `--suggested-fee-recipient` | The stored default
fee recipient stays. Without one anywhere, only keys with their own fee
recipient register before Gloas. |
| Any flag with a file or URL that has `default_config` | The source's
`default_config` wins whole. Overridden builder flags are named in a
warning; the fee recipient and gas limit flags are replaced silently.
Kept from today: with a version 1 file, `--suggested-gas-limit` still
sets the builder gas limit used for registrations. |
| Any flag with a file or URL without `default_config` | The flag
defaults stay and the source's per-key entries apply. |
| Per-key settings through the keymanager API | Win over every flag and
survive restarts, unless a file or URL with per-key entries is
configured, which replaces them. |


**Which issue(s) does this PR fix?**

Fixes #

author: Manu NALEPA
subject: Remove Bazel: Phase 4/9 (#17296)
body:
**What type of PR is this?**
Other

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**
This PR implements **Phase 4: Implement hermetic release binaries
build** of:
- https://github.com/OffchainLabs/prysm/issues/16982

The new `make dist` command allows the user to reproducibly build the
following binaries:`beacon-chain`, `validator`, `client-stats` and
`prysmctl` on the following platforms: `linux/amd64`, `linux/arm64`,
`darwin/amd64`, `darwin/arm64` and `windows/amd64`.

The `make help` output is now the following:

```
Prysm - Ethereum consensus client

Commands:
  make run <bin> [flags=...] [-- <args>]       Run a binary
  make build [<bin>...] [flags=...]            Build a binary (default: all)
  make gen [<kind>...] [mode=force|no-force]   Create generated code (default: all,no-force)
  make test [<kind>...] [mode=no-race|race]    Run unit tests (default: all,no-race)
  make e2e [<scenario>|<suite>...]             Run end-to-end tests (default: presubmit)
  make dist [<bin>...] [platform=...]          Build official release binaries (default: all,all platforms)
  make testdata                                Pre-fetch external spec-test data
  make clean                                   Clean everything
  make help                                    Show this help

Options:
  <bin>:           beacon-chain client-stats prysmctl validator
  gen <kind>:      proto ssz mocks
  test <kind>:     mainnet mainnet-spectest minimal minimal-spectest
  e2e <scenario>:  minimal builder web3signer slasher slashing scenario scenario-multiclient postmerge statediff mainnet multiclient
  e2e <suite>:
    presubmit:       minimal statediff slashing slasher
    postsubmit:      builder postmerge mainnet multiclient
    scenario_tests:  scenario scenario-multiclient
  dist <bin>:      beacon-chain validator client-stats prysmctl
  dist platform:   linux/amd64 linux/arm64 darwin/amd64 darwin/arm64 windows/amd64  (give one, or a space/comma list)

Notes:
  After '--', pass '--flag value' (not '--flag=value')
  'make dist SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH=<unix-seconds>' pins the build timestamp (reproducible build)
```

To build all binaries on all platforms, use `make dist`.
It will result in producing these binaries:
```
➜  dist ls
beacon-chain-v7.1.8-darwin-amd64  beacon-chain-v7.1.8-modern-darwin-amd64       client-stats-v7.1.8-darwin-amd64  client-stats-v7.1.8-windows-amd64.exe  prysmctl-v7.1.8-linux-arm64        validator-v7.1.8-linux-amd64
beacon-chain-v7.1.8-darwin-arm64  beacon-chain-v7.1.8-modern-linux-amd64        client-stats-v7.1.8-darwin-arm64  prysmctl-v7.1.8-darwin-amd64           prysmctl-v7.1.8-windows-amd64.exe  validator-v7.1.8-linux-arm64
beacon-chain-v7.1.8-linux-amd64   beacon-chain-v7.1.8-modern-windows-amd64.exe  client-stats-v7.1.8-linux-amd64   prysmctl-v7.1.8-darwin-arm64           validator-v7.1.8-darwin-amd64      validator-v7.1.8-windows-amd64.exe
beacon-chain-v7.1.8-linux-arm64   beacon-chain-v7.1.8-windows-amd64.exe         client-stats-v7.1.8-linux-arm64   prysmctl-v7.1.8-linux-amd64            validator-v7.1.8-darwin-arm64
```

To build a subset of binaries for a subset of platforms, you can specify
them.
For example the following command will only build the `beacon-chain` and
the `validator` binaries, for the `darwin/amd64` and the `windows/amd64`
platform:
```
make dist beacon-chain validator platform=darwin/amd64,windows/amd64
```

**How to test this pull request:**
On a given platform (example: `darwin/arm64`), run the following
command:
```
SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH=1781515081 make dist
```

On an other platform (example: `linux/amd64`), run the same command:
```
SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH=1781515081 make dist
```

Then, compare the content of the 2 `dist` directories:
```
diff <dist-1> <dist-2>
```

It should find absolutely **no** difference.

> [!NOTE]
> Pinning the date with the `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` environment variable is
needed for this test, because the build date is embedded in the
binaries. Without using this variable, the binaries will differ from a
few bytes corresponding to the embedded date.

**How does it work internally?**
`make dist` starts to build a Docker builder image
(`tools/cross-toolchain/Dockerfile.builder`).
When building this builder image, Docker installs in this image:
- The Zig cross toolchain (`install-zig.sh`). This will be used to build
Linux binaries.
- MinGW (`install-mingw.sh`). This will be used to build Windows
binaries.

author: terence
subject: Reject Gloas blocks whose bid does not build on the parent's execution head (#17575)
body:
Block gossip only checked the bid's parent block root and blob count, so
a block whose bid named an unknown parent block hash was accepted and
forwarded until the state transition caught it. This adds the missing
`[REJECT]` from `validate_beacon_block_gossip` using the same
`HasPayloadBlockHash` check the bid topic already applies.

Spec reference: https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/5294

author: terence
subject: Reject proposer preferences pointing past the shuffling dependent slot (#17484)
body:
- Adds the `[REJECT]` condition from
[consensus-specs#5582](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/5582)
to `proposer_preferences` gossip validation.
- Adds `compute_shuffling_dependent_slot` as
`slots.ShufflingDependentSlot`, clamped to the genesis slot for `epoch
<= MIN_SEED_LOOKAHEAD`.
- A dependent block at or after the start of the lookahead epoch cannot
be the block the shuffling depends on, so it is provably the sender's
fault.

author: Manu NALEPA
subject: Gloas: keep payload status right with several beacon nodes (#17585)
body:
**What type of PR is this?**
Bug fix


**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

**The issue:**

With several beacon nodes, the REST validator client could vote with a
beacon node that had not seen the payload yet:
- The payload attestation data only had to match the block root. A
beacon node that had the block but not the payload could win, and the
validator voted the payload absent.
- A beacon node announces a Gloas head twice: empty, then full. A slow
beacon node's "empty" event could overwrite a "full" head reported by
another beacon node, so the attestation data read preferred stale data.

 **The fix:**

- When a beacon node already announced the payload, only accept payload
attestation data with `payload_present` set.
- The head tracker no longer changes the same head from full back to
empty.

```
db88fd86fa06: Loading layer [==================================================>]  24.89MB/24.89MB
```

author: Preston Van Loon
subject: perf(state): avoid quadratic scans in multi-value-slice append (#17591)
body:
# Avoid quadratic scans in multi-value-slice append

**What type of PR is this?**

Performance improvement.

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

`multi-value-slice.Append` previously scanned existing appended
positions to find the next position for an object. Repeated appends
therefore rescanned an increasingly long prefix, causing quadratic work
when reconstructing a state with many appended validators.

Use the object's existing cached length to locate its next appended
position directly. Value sharing at that position, copy isolation,
detach/reuse behavior and locking are preserved. This removes the prefix
scan; it does not remove the checks among values sharing the destination
position.

This PR changes only the multi-value-slice implementation, its tests and
its changelog fragment. It is based directly on `develop` and has no
dependency on the historical-diff lookup PR or repair utility.

**Which issue(s) does this PR fix?**

No linked tracking issue. The original append loop was identified as a
dominant CPU bottleneck while reconstructing historical mainnet states.

**Other notes for review**

Tests exercise copied objects with shared and divergent values,
detach/reuse, a seeded operation model and concurrent appends to copied
objects. A benchmark measures batches of 1,000, 10,000 and 50,000
appends.

Independent validation on this PR's own tree, based on `develop` at
`9ad1bee498613b7c5d0b70c7d7d2f3c3536c5b16`:

- All five affected Bazel test targets executed successfully with
test-result caching disabled: KV, stategen, native state, hdiff and
multi-value-slice.
- gofmt, goimports, Gazelle and native `make build` passed. Native
checks used an isolated source archive with VCS stamping disabled to
avoid the existing generator scanning nested local workspaces.
- Release-mode Bazel builds of beacon-chain and validator passed.
- The multi-value-slice test suite also executed successfully with the
race detector.
- The release-mode append-scaling benchmark passed (`GOMAXPROCS=2`,
three measurements per size).

Earlier live-node testing had both this optimization and the separate
historical-diff lookup changes applied. Those endpoint timings are
combined evidence, not an isolated latency claim for this PR. This
change does not address missing historical records or alter database
serialization.

During self-review, the multi-value-slice suite was rerun uncached with
the race detector and `-test.count=10`; all repetitions passed.

Three fresh read-only historical API probes against the unchanged
combined live binary returned HTTP 200 and exactly matched prior
response payloads. The node remained synced. This is combined runtime
evidence, not an independent deployment of this branch.

Self-review found no blocking defect. I checked cached-length
maintenance across Init, Copy, Detach, UpdateAt and Reset, the
fresh-identifier native-state callers, destination value sharing and
locking. No source changes were needed.

Both branches merge cleanly into upstream `develop` at
`1ca08be9c5a31e8b8bcc331700facba173954f39`. The companion
historical-lookup fix is #17590; these are independent PRs, not a stack.
The full repository and network end-to-end suites were not run.

author: Preston Van Loon
subject: fix(db): replay missing historical hdiff states without repeated snapshot decoding (#17590)
body:
# Fix missing historical hdiff lookup and avoid repeated snapshot
decoding

Draft for author review; please leave in draft until the author requests
team review.

**What type of PR is this?**

Bug fix and historical-lookup performance improvement.

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

Historical state reads can fail with a generic missing-diff error even
when an earlier state and retained canonical blocks permit replay. This
PR classifies absent state, validator and balance diffs as
`ErrNotFoundState`, and translates absent snapshots at the
historical-read boundary so the existing replay path can recover.
Startup snapshot validation remains strict. Empty or undecodable diff
records are not reclassified as missing.

Every distinct ancestor diff is required; an empty cache level does not
make that ancestor optional. Required diffs are loaded before the full
snapshot, avoiding repeated large snapshot decodes during searches
across incomplete history.

The two commits separate correctness and lookup efficiency. This PR
contains no repair utility, database migration, persistent backfill or
multi-value-slice changes, and does not modify the historical-diff
writer.

**Which issue(s) does this PR fix?**

No linked tracking issue. The behavior was reproduced on a local mainnet
archive; the historical writer that created its gaps is unknown.

**Other notes for review**

Regression tests cover missing ancestor components, leaves and
snapshots, nonzero offsets, empty levels, malformed records, canonical
replay through a real database with state-root equality, and checking
missing diffs before decoding snapshots. A missing-history benchmark is
included.

Independent validation on this PR's own tree, based on `develop` at
`9ad1bee498613b7c5d0b70c7d7d2f3c3536c5b16`:

- All five affected Bazel test targets executed successfully with
test-result caching disabled: KV, stategen, native state, hdiff and
multi-value-slice.
- gofmt, goimports, Gazelle and native `make build` passed. Native
checks used an isolated source archive with VCS stamping disabled to
avoid the existing generator scanning nested local workspaces.
- Release-mode Bazel builds of beacon-chain and validator passed.
- The release-mode missing-history benchmark passed (`GOMAXPROCS=2`,
three measurements).

Earlier live validation used this change together with the separately
proposed append optimization. Those end-to-end timings must not be
attributed to this PR alone. Large gaps can still cause long ancestry
walks or replay; the March 2026 control exceeded 60 seconds in that
combined run. This PR does not persistently repair missing records.

During self-review, the KV and stategen Bazel suites were rerun uncached
and passed.

author: Manu NALEPA
subject: REST VC: wait past the attestation due time when no node has answered (#17620)
body:
**What type of PR is this?**
Bug fix

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**
**The issue**
When the REST validator client reads attestation data or a sync
committee block root, it stops at the hint deadline, which is the
attestation due time. If no beacon node has answered by then, for
example because a late block is still being processed, the read fails.
The attestation or sync committee message for that slot is then dropped.

**The fix**
When the caller's context has a deadline, it now bounds the read, and
the hint deadline becomes a fallback deadline:
- If a node returns a usable answer that does not match the announced
head, the read stops waiting for a matching answer at the hint deadline
and uses the usable one. This is the same as before.
- If no node has answered at all, the read keeps waiting, up to the
caller's deadline. A slow answer is better than no answer.

In `queryUntilAccepted`, the fallback deadline now also ends re-polling
and later rounds once a usable answer is in hand, not just the wait for
nodes that have not answered yet.

Without a caller deadline, nothing changes.
**Which issue(s) does this PR fix?**

Fixes:
- https://github.com/OffchainLabs/prysm/issues/17619

subject: Kurtosis+E2E: Add Assertoor playbooks that will replace legacy E2E evaluators (#17239)
body: **What type of PR is this?** > Other: E2E tests **What does this PR do? Why is it needed?** This PR adds a bunch of Assertoor playbooks that achieves the same level of assertions that we are doing with E2E evaluators. See [my document](https://hackmd.io/@junsong/rk5XHKUMzx#Evaluators) to check what evaluators are asserting at this moment. Most of diff come from newly added playbooks (YAML files), which will automatically add by `RegisterPlaybooks`. `RegisterPlaybooks` reads all `playbooks/*.yaml` files and register them via Assertoor API. Few playbooks use `run_javascript` to achieve parity with the legacy evaluators. Here's a brief index what each playbook do: - `blob-limits.yaml`: Replace `BlobLimitsRespected` evaluator. Send blob txs with large blob, and check for last 32 blocks whether each block includes blobs as we expected. - `blobs-included.yaml`: Replace `BlobsIncludedInBlocks` evaluator. Assumes `spamoor` is running in the enclave, and check whether each block includes blob or not. - `block-graffiti.yaml`: Replace `VerifyBlockGraffiti` evaluator. Check whether each block includes wanted graffiti pattern (`"^(Sushi|Ramen|Takoyaki)"`). Note that `"--graffiti-file=/config/graffiti.yaml"` is added in `minimal.yaml` (Kurtosis configuration). - `deposits.yaml`: Replace `ProcessesDepositsInBlocks` + `ActivatesDepositedValidators` + `DepositedValidatorsAreActive` + `testDepositsAndTx`. Test the full cycle for validator deposit process from sending deposit transaction to activate such validator. - `fee-recipient.yaml`: Replace `FeeRecipientIsPresent` evaluator. Check both EL and CL side: it asserts whether the balance of fee recipient is increased (EL side) and `fee_recipient` is a well-formed 20-byte address (CL side). - `fork-transition-*.yaml`: Replace `*ForkTransition` evaluators. Check the block version by fetching head block that the fork took place. - `metrics.yaml`: Replace `MetricsCheck` evaluator. Note that few functionality has been broken as #17043, so this playbook resurrects those assertions. Check this for full enclave lifecycle: - 1. Committee cache miss ratio is under 10%. - 2. Hot state cache miss ratio is under 10%. - 3. Failed aggregate-and-proof validations are under 80% of received messages. - 4. Failed attestation validations are under 15% of received messages. - `slashings.yaml`: Replace `InjectDoubleVoteOnEpoch` + `InjectDoubleBlockOnEpoch` + `ValidatorsSlashedAfterEpoch`. Test the full cycle of slashing both for attester and proposer. - `validators-active.yaml`: Replace `ValidatorsAreActive` evaluator. Check whether ALL validators (except the exited/withdrawn/slashed validators) from genesis are remaining active while the enclave is running. - `validators-sync-participation.yaml`: Replace `ValidatorSyncParticipation` evaluator. Check the sync committee participation is higher than 95%. - `voluntary-exits.yaml`: Replace `ProposeVoluntaryExit` + `ValidatorsHaveExited`. Test the full cycle of voluntary exits. - `withdrawals.yaml`: Replace `SubmitWithdrawal` + `ValidatorsHaveWithdrawn`. Test the full cycle of withdrawals. **Which issue(s) does this PR fix?** Part of **Phase 2: Parity with "minimal" test suites** - #15320 **Other notes for review** How to run a test: ``` bazel test //testing/endtoend:go_minimal_kurtosis_test \ --nocache_test_results --test_output=streamed ``` You can also check whether Assertoor is running well with Assertoor Web UI. After this PR got merged, #17247 is now ready for review. After merging #17247, we achieve a complete parity with legacy E2E test (`TestEndToEnd_MinimalConfig`). **Acknowledgements** - [x] I have read [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/prysmaticlabs/prysm/blob/develop/CONTRIBUTING.md). - [x] I have included a uniquely named [changelog fragment file](https://github.com/prysmaticlabs/prysm/blob/develop/CONTRIBUTING.md#maintaining-changelogmd). - [x] I have added a description with sufficient context for reviewers to understand this PR. - [x] I have tested that my changes work as expected and I added a testing plan to the PR description (if applicable). --------- Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context)

author: Jun Song
subject: Remove `BeaconState` proto message (#17535)
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

> Other: (Very nice) cleanup

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

This PR removes `beacon_state.proto` and automatically generated
`*.pb.go` files corresponds to it. Instead, we now replaces all proto
message definition of `BeaconState{Fork}` with native Go struct.

**Before**:

```proto
message BeaconState {
  // Versioning [1001-2000]
  uint64 genesis_time = 1001;
  // ... and so on
}
```

- Add new `BeaconState` per fork in `beacon_state.proto` file
- Run `make gen` for executing `protoc`, so that we have a Go struct.
- This system enforces us to have few converter functions from/to proto,
as well as slice type even though it is completely fine to use array
type for fixed bytevector.

**After**:

```go
// in beacon_state_mainnet.go
// BeaconState is the Phase0 SSZ state.
type BeaconState struct {
	GenesisTime                 uint64
	GenesisValidatorsRoot       []byte `ssz-size:"32"`
	Slot                        primitives.Slot
	Fork                        *Fork
	LatestBlockHeader           *BeaconBlockHeader
// and so on
```

- Add new `BeaconState` per fork in `beacon_state_{mainnet|minimal}.go`
file
- No need to generate `*.pb.go` files related to the state. Plus we
remove over 9K lines of generated files which is awesome.
- Note that we don't need few entries in `ssz_proto_library.bzl` as it
is now natively maintained in native Go struct definition.

**Which issue(s) does this PR fix?**

Fixes https://github.com/OffchainLabs/prysm/issues/17503

**Other notes for review**

### How to review this PR

This PR is designed to review commit by commit. It consists of three
parts:

#### Revisit the testing harness

Until [fix(ssz): derive query field names without json
tags](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/prysm/pull/17535/commits/1d108c7df7ce5706143346267706dd69ba884bf2),
these are collections of groundwork for the later work. First commit
([test(state): support non-protobuf states in SSZ
harness](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/prysm/pull/17535/commits/e5684be8e28493ceab7f06ebb15fed5fd07da825))
is note-worthy - as it touches our equality check. Main purpose is
dropping proto dependency on equality check.

#### Mechanical change from Altair to Gloas, and then Phase0

From [refactor(state): replace Altair protobuf with SSZ
struct](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/prysm/pull/17535/commits/27f63deac9d8f5e7f5e88b022d94d32c850fa03b)
to [refactor(state): replace Phase0 protobuf with SSZ
struct](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/prysm/pull/17535/commits/4d8c2f5c6087e4f8df7db7d5c2c36bfb29bce9d8),
each commit mechanically migrates to native struct per fork. Most of the
diff of each commit is regenerated `*.pb.go` files and some equality
check in our spectest runner.

Phase0 is deliberately done after Gloas as it has different wire format
and pattern when saving in the storage.

#### Cleanups

From [refactor(state): drop protobuf from
beacon-chain/state](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/prysm/pull/17535/commits/217be0feaabf9456e5a2b0fea1be9349cd5ba77f),
commits are mostly cleaning things up which are now unused or dead.
[refactor(proto): remove
beacon_state.proto](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/prysm/pull/17535/commits/69d9f54a3694b2a89a7f26cf999cbb135083a22d)
is note-worthy, as it retires `beacon_state.proto` and moves each proto
message into separate parts in the codebase, so please read the
description.

### Production Risk

Before #17523, there was a very tiny production risk on DB migration,
but now we don't have. I _believe_ this PR doesn't bring any production
risk and should work well without any problems, but here's some notes:

- DB compatability: We save `BeaconState` in SSZ format, so it doesn't
need to be considered. Same behavior.
- `CopySlice(nil)` returns `nil` instead of `[]`.
- SSZ Query package changes are not considered as production IMO.

### Follow-ups

- Move state-related definition and function into dedicated package.
`proto/` package is not proper location now.
- Rename `*Proto*` methods. I deliberately omitted it in this PR because
it covers almost entire codebase.
- Delegate SSZ List limit and SSZ Vector length to `fieldparams`
configuration which is considered as canonical.
- Better memory allocation and no more Proto conversion.
- As `methodical-ssz` doesn't support yet for array type, we need a
patch there.

author: kasey
subject: Enforce ProgressiveList limits defined on STF during unmarshal (#17412)
body: ## Background and rationale EIP-7688 and EIP-7916 define a replacement for the `List` family of ssz collection types supporting progressive merkleization: ProgressiveList, ProgressiveBitlist, ProgressiveByteList. Unlike the base ssz design, progressive collection types do not have a strict maximum size defined in their spec type definition. Previously the definition not only changed how the fields were merkleized, but also moved validation as early in the p2p pipeline as possible, to happen at the unmarshal step. We still have limits we want to enforce (e.g. `MAX_ATTESTATIONS_ELECTRA`), but those limit checks have migrated from the unmarshal step to a validation function on the STF. When upstream specs moved to this scheme, spectest generators stopped limiting the size of test inputs according to the limits, requiring implementations to accept inputs that were outside the bounds. In prysm's codegen we dropped the validation previously performed at the unmarshal step to accept these fixtures. However this change unnecessarily defers validation that we could perform up front, potentially spreading the responsibility for checking these lengths to various parts of the application in ways that could lead to bugs. It could also open us up to limited griefing from malicious inputs that cause extra memory allocation for values that the decoder can easily determine are invalid. So I've asked @jtraglia for a compromise: modify specs so that spectest generation is aware of the valid range of values for these types with limits enforced at the STF, so that fixtures can avoid exceeding those ranges. That allows us to pass ssz-static spectests using types where we have restored input size validation to our unmarshal methods. This also gives spectest generators a convenient place to pick a size for values to exceed in fixtures where the STF checks are being tested (the spectest generator can use `> $LIMIT` for invalid inputs, and `== $LIMIT` for valid inputs). The upstream changes are in [consensus-specs PR 5564](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/5564). This PR should update to the version pin including that PR once it merges (and will fail with length validation errors in the meantime). **Acknowledgements** - [x] I have read [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/prysmaticlabs/prysm/blob/develop/CONTRIBUTING.md). - [x] I have included a uniquely named [changelog fragment file](https://github.com/prysmaticlabs/prysm/blob/develop/CONTRIBUTING.md#maintaining-changelogmd). - [x] I have added a description with sufficient context for reviewers to understand this PR. - [x] I have tested that my changes work as expected and I added a testing plan to the PR description (if applicable). --- Stack created with GitHub Stacks CLI • Give Feedback 💬 --------- Co-authored-by: Kasey Kirkham Co-authored-by: Potuz Co-authored-by: james-prysm <90280386+james-prysm@users.noreply.github.com>

author: Manu NALEPA
subject: Postpone the validator client shutdown until a restart misses no rewarded duty (#17616)
body:
**What type of PR is this?**
Feature

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**
Postpone the validator client shutdown until a restart misses no
rewarded duty

#### The issue
A restarted validator client only performs the duties of slots starting
after it is ready. But on SIGINT or SIGTERM, the validator client stops
right away, whatever the moment in the slot. So even a quick restart can
cut off the duties in progress, or miss the duties of the next slot.

#### The feature
On the first interrupt, the validator client keeps running until a
restart
would not miss any rewarded duty:
1. If the current slot has rewarded duties, it waits for them to be
done.
2. Then it shuts down if at least 3 seconds are left before the next
slot,
    or if the next slot has no rewarded duty.
3. Otherwise, it waits for the next slot, and checks again.

Rewarded duties are attestations, sync committee messages and block
proposals (including the Gloas self-build envelope). Aggregations, sync
committee contributions and payload attestations earn no reward, so they
are not waited for.

A second interrupt shuts down immediately.

```
--disable-duty-aware-shutdown      Stop the validator client immediately on SIGINT/SIGTERM, instead of waiting for the moment in the slot where a restart would not miss any rewarded duty. (default: false)
```
restores the previous behavior.

**How to test it**

**Case 1: No rewarded duty in the current slot or the next slot**
Stop the validator client. It should stop immediately.

**Case 2: Some not yet done rewarded duty in the current slot.
(Typically, `ctrl-c` in the first 4 seconds of the slot where a
validator has to attest in the current slot)**

Stop the validator client. Is should wait for the duty to be done before
shutting down.
```
[2026-10-04 20:09:36.39]  INFO node: Got interrupt, shutting down...
[2026-10-04 20:09:36.39]  INFO client: Waiting for the rewarded duties of the slot to be done before shutting down. Interrupt again to shut down immediately slot=15360046
...
[2026-10-04 20:09:37.43]  INFO client: Submitted new attestations blockRoot=0x125d9aee6685 committeeIndices=[25 6] pubkeys=[xxxx] sinceSlotStartTime=2.433s slot=15360046 sourceEpoch=480000 sourceRoot=0xd3df2690cbbd targetEpoch=480001 targetRoot=0x36de206d0177
[2026-10-04 20:09:37.43]  INFO client: Stopping service
[2026-10-04 20:09:37.43]  INFO client: Context canceled, stopping validator
[2026-10-04 20:09:37.43]  INFO client: Validator service context canceled, stopping
[2026-10-04 20:09:37.43]  INFO node: Stopping Prysm validator
```

**Case 3: Trying to stop the validator client too late in slot N, while
slot N+1 has some rewarded duties. (Typically, `ctrl-c` in the last 3
seconds of the slot where a validator has to attest during the next
slot)**
```
[10:11 PM][2026-10-04 20:10:46.06]  INFO node: Got interrupt, shutting down...
[2026-10-04 20:10:46.06]  INFO client: Too late in the slot to restart before the next one, waiting for the rewarded duties of the next slot to be done before shutting down. Interrupt again to shut down immediately slot=15360051 timeLeftBeforeNextSlot=932ms
...
[2026-10-04 20:10:48.90]  INFO client: Submitted new attestations blockRoot=0xdfcf873c1ae7 committeeIndices=[59] pubkeys=[xxx] sinceSlotStartTime=1.908s slot=15360052 sourceEpoch=480000 sourceRoot=0xd3df2690cbbd targetEpoch=480001 targetRoot=0x36de206d0177
```

subject: Apply gossip clock disparity to Gloas payload attestation, bid, and proposer preferences slot checks (#17576)
body:
The Gloas gossip slot checks for payload attestations, bids, and
proposer preferences compared raw slot numbers, so honest messages
arriving within `MAXIMUM_GOSSIP_CLOCK_DISPARITY` of a slot boundary were
ignored. This adds a shared `withinSlotRange` helper mirroring the
spec's `is_within_slot_range` and uses it for `is_current_slot`,
`is_current_or_next_slot`, and `is_past_slot`.

Spec reference: https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/5294

author: terence
subject: Read head and forkchoice node under one lock in GetAttestationData (#17633)
body:
`GetAttestationData` read the cached head before taking the forkchoice
lock, which block import holds through `saveHead`. A request arriving
mid import got head N-1 with block N's payload bit and voted one slot
stale. On Sepolia after Gloas this hit 7% of requests on the node that
imports last.

Read the head and the canonical forkchoice node under one forkchoice
read lock, so a mid-import request waits for the import and returns N
with N's bit.

author: Manu NALEPA
subject: Replace the per-call `Broadcasted data column sidecars` debug log with a `Broadcasted data column sidecars summary` log, aggregated per block root and emitted once no column was broadcast for this root during 100 ms. (#17642)
body:
**What type of PR is this?**
Feature

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

Since partial data columns are enabled by default, nodes log many
`Broadcasted data column sidecars` debug lines with `count=1`. A single
slot could produces one line per custody column:


[2026-10-07 22:33:12.30] DEBUG p2p: Broadcasted data column sidecars
summary count=8 indices=18,46,69,71,92-93,116,121 root=0x57ea81eb...
sinceStartTime=[min: 203.84536ms, avg: 204.182433ms, max: 204.700129ms]
slot=11306566

**Before, without partial columns:**
`engine_getBlobsV2` was all or nothing.
- If the execution client has all the blobs, the node builds all its
custody columns at once and broadcasts them in a **single call**: one
**single, grouped** log line per block.
- Otherwise, the node gets full columns from gossip. gossipsub forwards
them itself, and Prysm logs nothing.

**Now, with partial data columns enabled by default:**
`engine_getBlobsV3` can return only some of the blobs. The node then
publishes partial columns, and peers send the missing cells. Each column
is on its own gossip topic, so each one is completed at a different
moment. When a column is complete, the node re-broadcasts it as a full
sidecar for peers that don't support partial messages. That broadcast
holds one column, so it logs one `count=1` line.

This pull request groups broadcasts per block root and write one
`Broadcasted data column sidecars summary` line per root. The line is
written once no column has been broadcast for that root for 100 ms. The
format matches the already existing `Accepted data column sidecars
summary` log.

DEBUG p2p: Broadcasted data column sidecars summary count=8
indices=18,46,69,71,92,93,116,121 root=0x… sinceStartTime=[min: 216ms,
avg: 260ms, max: 284ms] slot=11305599

author: Manu NALEPA
subject: Use the slot deadline for the duties of the first slot of an epoch (#17637)
body:
**What type of PR is this?**
Bug fix

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**
**The issue**
At the first slot of an epoch, the runner overwrites `deadline` with the
deadline of the last slot of the epoch, to give more time to the duties
update. The context of the duties of the slot is then created from this
overwritten value, so these duties may run until the end of the epoch
instead of the end of the slot.

**The fix**
The duties update uses its own `dutiesDeadline` variable, so `deadline`
stays the deadline of the slot.

subject: Unfinalized checkpoint sync (#17559)
body:
This PR fakes a finalized checkpoint on forkchoice and allows the node
to start from an arbitrary state.

Tested on KT as follows: 

- Start a run with 7 nodes, 3 prysm, 2 Lighthouse, 2 Lodestar. 
- Wait for finalization. 
- Stop the PRysm nodes. 
- Wait 6 epochs without finalizing. 
- Grab a checkpoint state from either LH or Lodestar. 
- Restart the Prysm nodes with an empty db and from the unfinalized
checkpoint.

The node immediately catches up and starts attesting.

author: Potuz
subject: Archive mode: backfill to a past state and regenerate history into the hdiff tree (#17292)
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

Feature

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

Adds `--enable-archive`, which turns a checkpoint-synced node into an
archive node: it backfills blocks down to an origin state and then
replays forward, persisting a state at every state-diff tree boundary.
The result is a node that can serve any historical state from the origin
to the head at hdiff speed, without a from-genesis resync.

This implements the `state_diff.md` §Backfill design, which was written
down but unimplemented (`--backfill-origin-state` and
`--pruner-retention-snapshots` had no code behind them).

```
--enable-archive                                    # origin defaults to genesis
--enable-archive --archive-origin-state state.ssz   # or start from a past state
```

`--enable-archive` implies `--enable-state-diff` and
`--enable-backfill`.

### Why the tree offset has to move

`getBaseAndDiffChain` reconstructs slot *s* from the level-0 snapshot at
*s - (s-o) mod 2^λ_0*, and slots below the offset *o* have no
representation at all. A checkpoint-synced node sets *o* to the
checkpoint slot, so it can never represent anything older. Archive mode
anchors the tree at the archive origin instead, which has three
consequences:

- `initArchiveOrigin` runs before `startDB`, so it sets the offset
before `SaveGenesisData` or `SaveOrigin` can. Those two become no-ops
for the offset in archive mode; non-archive behaviour is unchanged.
- The checkpoint origin state's slot is generally not a boundary of the
re-anchored tree, so `SaveOrigin` persists it as a root-keyed hot
snapshot. `State`/`HasState` consult that bucket first, which is what
keeps stategen and backfill able to find it.
- The live chain's level-0 anchor now lies in the not-yet-regenerated
past, so `MigrateToCold` genuinely *cannot* write diffs until the walk
reaches it. Suppression is a correctness requirement here, not a
simplification. `ForceCheckpoint` (which runs on every graceful
shutdown) is routed to a hot snapshot for the same reason.

### The walk

New `beacon-chain/archive` package. Waits for backfill, then replays
forward from the origin state, carrying the working state in memory and
writing one state per tree boundary — it never reads the tree back,
which is what keeps it tractable. Progress lives in a new
`ArchiveStatus` record next to the offset metadata, so a restart resumes
at the last written boundary. Every boundary is written, including those
whose slot had no block: a hole in a level makes every deeper read
inside that span unresolvable.

When every boundary at or below the finalized checkpoint exists, it
hands migration back under `migrationLock`.

### Two supporting changes that matter at mainnet scale

- **Anchor memo** (`stateDiffCache`): `getAnchor` deserialized a full
state on every call. An anchor is reused for every slot in its span, so
a mainnet walk at the default `exponents[last]=5` paid ~410k full state
deserializations. Now memoized per level and invalidated on replacement.
- **Restart resume snapshots**: while regeneration runs, a full state is
snapshotted by root every 2048 slots. Without this, a restart replays
from the sync origin and the cost grows without bound, because
`finalizedInfo` never advances. This is deliberately independent of
`saveHotStateDB` — `checkSaveHotStateDB` turns that mode off on every
block while finality is healthy.

**Which issue(s) does this PR fix?**

None filed.

**Other notes for review**

Draft: **not yet exercised on a live devnet.** The remaining
verification is a two-node devnet comparison (state roots at a level-0
boundary, a deepest-level boundary, and a skip-slot boundary), plus
restarts mid-backfill and mid-regeneration. Reviewing the design in the
meantime is useful.

Three things worth a reviewer's attention:

1. **The origin state is trust input**, exactly like
`--checkpoint-state`. Startup only checks slot alignment and the genesis
validators root; the real verification is the state-root comparison on
the first replayed block, which can only happen after backfill
completes. A bad origin means deleting the database. Documented in
`state_diff.md`.
2. **Gloas envelopes**: the walk reuses `ProcessBlockForStateRoot`
exactly as `stategen`'s replay path does. That path applies no envelopes
today (`CanonicalHistory.executionPayloadEnvelope` is dead code), so
Gloas regeneration inherits that existing gap rather than fixing it.
3. **Sizing**: cost is dominated by the last exponent. At the default 5
a mainnet archive stores ~410k per-epoch diffs and `diffToBalances`
allocates a `len(balances)`-sized `[]int64` per diff. `state_diff.md`
now tells operators to raise it unless they want per-epoch resolution.
Archive mode is rejected together with `--beacon-db-pruning`.

Also fixed along the way: `populateStateDiffCacheFromDB` cached the
level-0 anchor at the offset unconditionally, which is the wrong era
once the tree spans more than `2^exponents[0]` slots (self-corrected via
a warning + reload, but now correct up front).

**Testing plan**

Unit tests added for: offset re-basing (archive keeps it, non-archive
still re-anchors), the `SaveOrigin` snapshot path, the frontier guard
including the one boundary the walk itself writes, the anchor memo and
its invalidation, the `das` block floor precedence and slot-0 clamp,
`MigrateToCold`/`ForceCheckpoint`/`DisableSaveHotStateToDB` suppression,
the lagging-frontier handoff refusal, and the walk itself — every
regenerated boundary state is compared against the real chain state,
including across a skipped slot and across a resume.


`beacon-chain/{archive,db/...,state/stategen,das,rpc/lookup,node,sync/...}`,
`config/features` and `cmd/beacon-chain/...` all pass.
`beacon-chain/rpc/prysm/v1alpha1/beacon` fails on `develop` too
(`Slashings` length 8192 vs 64), unrelated.

Devnet verification still outstanding, as noted above.

author: kasey
subject: Optimize ExecutionPayload Transactions representation (#17584)
body:
# ExecutionPayload.Transactions Optimization

Currently we represent the Transactions list in an ExecutionPayload as
2D byte array (`[][]byte`). We don't need to interact with the
individual transactions other than to ensure they are non-zero values,
so the overhead of looping over and allocating slices for the individual
txns when unmarshaling, marshaling and merkleizing is really not worth
it. We can avoid quite a bit of computation, gc pressure etc etc by just
validating the encoded form of the bytes list and keeping it in that
representation for all operations in the beacon node and validator. This
PR adds a custom type for the transactions list to accomplish that goal
and makes the necessary changes across the grpc boundary to support the
change.

## Note re Backwards-Compatibility

Both the struct generated by protoc and the wire format of
ExecutionPayload will change with this PR.

### Wire format

At the level of the wire format, this represents a breaking change. A
new protobuf field number was used for the new tx list format, and the
old field will be ignored by the beacon node. This means that validators
running releases without this change, expecting the old wire format and
unaware of the new field, need to be protected from accidentally signing
an empty transaction list.

The change only impacts the gloas `ExecutionPayload`; pre-gloas types
are unaffected. To ensure that we fail loudly if a validator tries to
interact with gloas endpoints using the old method/schema, a new grpc
endpoint version (v2) was added, and the v1 version will return an error
when the validator requests a payload. The intention is to force
validators to upgrade if attempting to connect to an incompatible node.

For any networks that haven't forked into gloas yet (mainnet and all
testnets except Sepolia), this change should have no impact. However
special care should be taken in Sepolia. Ideally operators will get new
beacon nodes running on the release including this change, then restart
validators with the new version to point at the upgraded nodes. Upgraded
validators talking to old beacon nodes will get an error due to the
unknown v2 route, and any validator (particularly un-upgraded ones)
talking to upgraded nodes will get an error if attempting to use the v1
gloas methods.

### If your code interacts with the struct (unlikely!)

I believe few if any users of prysm have custom code interacting with
the go struct. Any code that does will be impacted and should be updated
to use the `TransactionListBuilder` for initializing or mutating
transactions lists, and the `Transactions() [][]byte` helper for reading
them. The latter returns slices that are shared references to the
underlying data byte slice, which is fine for prysm's purposes as we
never mutate these values, but other users should take care to copy
values if this mutation would be harmful. You can use the test support
methods in this PR as an example of how to use the builder for
populating the transactions slice.

author: Potuz
subject: Verify gossip payload envelope signatures without loading state (#17652)
body:
**What type of PR is this?**

Bug fix

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

Gossip validation of execution payload envelopes retrieved the block's
verifying state (`blockVerifyingState`) before checking the envelope
signature. For blocks whose state is not cached (e.g. older unfinalized
blocks), this triggers a state replay for every envelope received, even
ones with an invalid signature.

The signature only needs a pubkey and a domain, so this PR removes the
state retrieval:

- The forkchoice `Node` now records the bid's builder pubkey
(`*[48]byte`, nil for self-built and pre-Gloas blocks). It is set from
the post-state in `InsertNode`, and via
`BlockAndCheckpoints.BuilderPubkey` in `InsertChain` (filled in batch
sync).
- Self-built envelopes are verified against the proposer's pubkey
(`block.ProposerIndex()`) from the head state. Validator index to pubkey
is consistent across branches since validators are only added from
finalized deposits.
- Builder envelopes are verified against the pubkey stored in
forkchoice. Builder indices can be reused across branches, so the head
state can't be used for these.
- New `VerifySignatureWithPubkey` on the envelope verifier computes the
domain from the fork schedule at the envelope's epoch and the genesis
validators root.
- If no pubkey is available, the envelope is ignored (not rejected).
- The builder pubkey is cleared once the full node is created
(`InsertPayload`, `MarkFullNode`, `InsertChain` with `HasPayload`), and
gossip envelopes whose root already has a full node are ignored early.

**Which issue(s) does this PR fix?**

**Other notes for review**

- `fillInForkChoiceMissingBlocks` and the startup forkchoice rebuild
don't have per-block post-states, so they leave the builder pubkey nil;
builder envelopes for those blocks are ignored on gossip.
- `InsertNode` skips setting the pubkey if the state lookup fails (e.g.
Gloas genesis) instead of failing insertion.

author: Manu NALEPA
subject: Backfill: Fix Gloas (#17632)
body:
**What type of PR is this?**
Bug fix

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**
There is some issues with backfill on Gloas.
This PR contains multiple commits. Each commit is a fix of a specific
issue.
The corresponding commit message explains the issue and the fix.

**Other notes for review**
To reproduce the issue, just run the `--backfill` flag on Sepolia.
You'll get something like [these
logs](https://gist.github.com/nalepae/716eb538d94dd71b80237c193f974382).

```
[2026-10-06 19:40:13.17] DEBUG backfill: Backfill batch failed to import batchId=11298368:11298400 begin=11298368 blobPid= blockPid=16Uiu2HAkyewYrfxiSkZFCgqZr5uCMcbFUcCArbPHMBj7tADM5w44 busyPid=16Uiu2HAkyewYrfxiSkZFCgqZr5uCMcbFUcCArbPHMBj7tADM5w44 colPid= end=11298400 error=IsDataAvailable: column store availability check failed: entry filter: root=&0xf9804a89181daebe324d221b3d709e147527da76ef46e7e20ba8217d702be1a3, index=0x5: no sidecar in cache for block commitment retries=131 retryAfter=2026-10-06 19:40:11.668479912 +0000 UTC m=+286.427116517 scheduled=2026-10-06 19:40:10.668541072 +0000 UTC m=+285.427177637 seq=390 state=importable
```

After the fix, the backfill should run smoothly.

Tested ✅ on 2 full (Gloas + Fulu transition) Sepolia backfills.

Copy of the commit messages.

**Backfill: Do not check columns of Gloas blocks with an empty payload**
The issue
On Gloas, when the payload of a block is never revealed, the block has
no
data columns. Backfill knows this: it does not download columns for such
a
block, and peers do not serve them anyway.

However, the data availability check still requires columns for every
block
with blob commitments in its bid. The check fails with "no sidecar in
cache
for block commitment", the batch is retried forever, and backfill is
stuck.

The fix
When building the column batch, record which blocks have an empty
payload.
The availability check then skips these blocks, the same way backfill
skips
downloading their columns.

**Backfill: Decide the payload of the last block of a batch once its
child is known**
The issue
On Gloas, backfill finds out whether the payload of a block was revealed
by
looking at its child. The child of the last block of a batch is in the
batch
above, so backfill could not see it and assumed the payload was
revealed.

When that payload was in fact empty, backfill kept asking peers for the
columns of this block. Peers never serve columns of a block with an
empty
payload, so the batch never finished and backfill was stuck.

The fix
The payload of the last block of a batch is now undecided until its
child is
known. Backfill does not wait for the columns of an undecided block, but
keeps
them if peers send them.

The child is the lowest block already backfilled. Backfill reads it from
the
database when the batch is built, if the batch above is already
imported, and
otherwise when the batch is imported. Then:
- if the payload is empty, the columns of the block are not checked;
- if the payload is full and its columns are missing, the import fails
and
  the batch is retried, this time downloading the columns.

author: Potuz
subject: Use the target's shuffling dependent root in getRecentPreState (#17649)
body:
### Problem

`getRecentPreState` decides whether the head state can validate an
attestation for checkpoint `c` by comparing
`DependentRootForEpoch(headRoot, headEpoch-1)` against
`DependentRootForEpoch(c.Root, headEpoch-1)`.
`DependentRootForEpoch(root, E)` returns the last block before epoch
`E`.

The committees of `c.Epoch` are fixed by the last block before
`c.Epoch-1`. The current comparison is only correct when `c.Epoch ==
headEpoch`:

- **`c.Epoch == headEpoch-1`:** it compares the last block before
`c.Epoch`, which is one epoch too strict.
- Example: head in epoch 11, attestation target `{10, R@slot 303}` from
a node that didn't see R310.
- The head chain's last block of epoch 9 is R310 while the target's is
R303, so the check fails.
- Epoch 10's committees only depend on the last block of epoch 8, which
both chains share, so the head state was usable and we needlessly
regenerated a state.
- **`c.Epoch == headEpoch+1`:** it compares the last block before
`c.Epoch-2`, which is one epoch too loose. This was only safe because
the function also required `c.Root == headRoot`.

### Fix

- Compare `DependentRootForEpoch(·, c.Epoch-1)` for both roots. This is
exactly the block that fixes `c.Epoch`'s shuffling, for every `c.Epoch`
that reaches the check: `headEpoch-1`, `headEpoch` or `headEpoch+1`.
- Since the comparison is now exact for the next epoch, return the head
state without advancing it whenever the fork version doesn't change,
even if `c.Root != headRoot`.
- `c.Root == headRoot` is still required before the path that advances
the head state with `ProcessSlotsIfNeeded` and caches it under `c`.
- If the head is several epochs behind the target, both dependent roots
resolve to the roots themselves. The check then already implies `c.Root
== headRoot`.

### Why equal dependent roots are reliable

Both lookups go through forkchoice. A root that isn't in forkchoice
returns `ErrNilNode`, and we fall back to the slow path. Let `F` be the
finalized block (the root of the forkchoice tree) and `E = c.Epoch-1`.

**The dependent block is not finalized.** That is, it's at or after `F`,
so it's still a forkchoice node.
- Forkchoice walks each chain's target pointers back to that exact node.
- Equal results mean both chains share the same last block before
`start(E)`.
- Different results mean the shufflings may really differ, and we fall
back.

This includes chains that branch off `F` before the finalized epoch's
start because of skipped slots. Example: finalized `{9, R280}` with a
late sibling R285, a child of R280. R285 is a real node, so its lookup
returns R285 while the canonical chain returns R280, and the comparison
fails as it should.

**The dependent block is finalized.** That is, `F` is at or after
`start(E)`.
- The last block before `start(E)` is a strict ancestor of `F`.
- Every node in forkchoice descends from `F`, so both chains share that
block, and the shuffling is the same.
- Forkchoice answers either with `finalizedDependentRoot` (the parent of
`F`) or with a zero root, if the walk reaches `F` after pruning cleared
its target. Both lookups follow the same path through `F`, so they
return the same value.
- If they ever disagreed, the result is a false negative, i.e. the slow
path, never a wrong state.

In both cases a match is never wrong; at worst we miss a chance to use
the head state.

### Why the head state is valid

Every caller of `AttestationTargetState` uses the returned state only
for the following. None of them reads balances, proposer data, sync
committees or the PTC.
- the committees of `c.Epoch` (`BeaconCommitteeFromState` /
`AttestationCommitteesFromState`);
- the active validator count, for the committee count and subnet;
- validator public keys;
- `Fork()` and `GenesisValidatorsRoot()` for signature domains.

**Committees.** `compute_committee` depends only on the seed and on
`get_active_validator_indices(state, c.Epoch)`, not on balances.
- **Seed:** it uses the randao mix of epoch `c.Epoch-2`, which is final
after the last block before `start(c.Epoch-1)`. That's exactly the block
we compare. Later blocks only change the mixes for later epochs, and the
mixes buffer keeps 65536 epochs, so the head state still has it.
- **Active set:** any activation, exit, slashing or consolidation
processed after that block gets an epoch of at least `current + 1 +
MAX_SEED_LOOKAHEAD`, which is after `c.Epoch`. New deposits are appended
as inactive. So the active set at `c.Epoch` is the same on both chains.

**Range of epochs.**
- `c.Epoch` is the head state's previous or current epoch: the mix and
the registry are already in the state.
- `c.Epoch` is the next epoch: the mix for `c.Epoch-2 = headEpoch-1` is
already final in the head state. We only return it unadvanced when the
fork version doesn't change at the boundary.

**Public keys.** Validator indices and keys never change. Every member
of a `c.Epoch` committee exists at the same index with the same key in
both registries.

**Signature domain.** `get_domain` uses `fork.previous_version` for
epochs before `fork.epoch`. So a head state one epoch ahead, even right
after a fork, gives the correct domain for the target's epoch. The
genesis validators root is the same on both chains.
